articles.title: Football: Why are some shin pads so small?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team explore why some football shin pads are so small, and what the laws are around wearing them.
articles.body:
Liverpool 's Lewis Koumas made his full Premier League debut against Manchester City on Sunday.

While doing so, he sported some very low socks over what appeared to be a very small shin pad.

Last season, images of Burnley's Marcus Edwards went viral after the 27-year-old was seen wearing barely visible shin pads during a Premier League match against West Ham.

Two years ago, a picture of teenager Harry Howell celebrating with James Milner while they were Brighton team-mates also gained attention after fans noticed the visible difference in the size of their shin pads.

Howell's 'micro' pair were an obvious contrast to Milner's far more traditional-sized guards.

So what is behind the trend of extra-small shin guards, and why are they used instead of regular-sized pairs?

The simple answer is that players can choose what size shin pads they want to wear.

The International Football Association Board (Ifab), responsible for the laws of the game, say that shin pads are a mandatory piece of equipment players must wear while playing.

Be of an appropriate size to provide reasonable protection and be covered by the socks

And players are responsible for the size and suitability of their shin pads

The law does not define what an "appropriate" shin pad size is, but leave that decision to each individual player.

Shin pads provide vital protection for players to prevent serious injuries.

There has been a rising trend in younger footballers, as well as some big stars, wearing small shin pads during matches.

The reason for this could be for more comfort and to allow players to move around with greater ease.

Referees are only required to check that some form of shin guards are being worn, Ifab told BBC Sport.

Ifab said players - or the parents or guardians of youth players - must take responsibility for their own safety on the pitch.

While shin pad size is ultimately an individuals choice, any decisions around player safety would also be made in consultation with their club and medical staff.

Grassroots football teams have started to ban small shin pads for safety reasons.

There are concerns that small shin pads do not cover the shins properly, which can lead to an increased risk of injury - especially at non-elite level.

In August 2024, a football club banned small shin pads after a youth player suffered a double leg break.

Penistone Church player Alfie Collins broke his tibia and fibula in a tackle during a game. The teenager's shin pads, which were no bigger than a credit card, were similar to a size recently worn by some stars of the professional game.

Shin pads "play an important role in injury prevention as they are intended to protect the shin from injury", the Football Association said.

"'Micro' or 'mini' shin pads may therefore increase the risk of injury due to the smaller amount of shin covered compared to larger sized shin pads," they added.

articles.title: Tiago Santos: Lille consider legal action after defender's serious knee injury against Le Havre
articles.summary: The club have described the tackle on defender Tiago Santos as 'uncontrolled and dangerous'.
articles.body:
French club Lille say they are considering taking legal action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a knee injury from an "uncontrolled and dangerous" tackle against Le Havre on Saturday.

Santos, 24, was carried off on a stretcher having ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), as well as suffering a meniscal tear in his right knee.

He was tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson in the first half of Lille's eventual 1-0 win and, while it was given as a foul, Richardson did not receive a yellow or red card for the challenge.

Lille said they have asked the league to refer the incident to its disciplinary panel, believing it should have been a red card because the tackle was made "from behind, uncontrolled and in a dangerous manner".

"Beyond the injury itself, the circumstances in which it occurred and the lack of sanction raise serious questions for the club," the club's statement added.

The star is Luis Enrique - inside the plans to keep PSG at the top

"LOSC has referred the matter to the French Football Federation and the Professional Football League in order to obtain an examination of the handling of this action by the refereeing team and the video assistance.

"LOSC is studying the possible remedies and reserves the right to take any legal action to obtain compensation for its damages."

The club said Santos will be unable to play for "several months".

Le Havre responded by saying that the club and Richardson expressed their support for Santos in his recovery, but backed the decision of the match referee and the video assistant referee.

They also questioned Lille's move to "punish its player after the fact, since such a decision would fall outside the current regulations".

"HAC respects all fellow Ligue 1 clubs and expects the same respect in return," Le Havre added.

BBC Sport has contacted the LFP, which runs the French professional leagues, for comment.

Lille are second in Ligue 1 and face Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday.

articles.title: Dani Carvajal ya está en Getafe: “Ojalá salga todo bien y podamos estar aquí”
articles.standfirst: El futbolista ultima en las oficinas azulonas su contrato y se pondrá a las órdenes de Bordalás
articles.summary: El futbolista ultima en las oficinas azulonas su contrato y se pondrá a las órdenes de Bordalás
articles.body: Dani Carvajal ha llegado en la mañana del martes a Getafe. El lateral derecho aterrizó en las oficinas azulonas para ultimar los detalles de su contrato y firmar con el club del sur de Madrid, a priori, hasta final de temporada. “Vamos a ver cómo están los contratos. Ojalá que salga todo bien y podamos estar aquí”, decía el futbolista a su llegada ante los micrófonos de DAZN. Carvajal llega libre tras acabar su contrato el pasado mes de junio con el Real Madrid y podría incluso ponerse a las órdenes de Bordalás este mismo martes, aunque no podrá jugar el jueves en Craiova al no poder ser inscrito para la Conference. Donde sí podría debutar es en el Coliseum, en LaLiga, el lunes frente al Rayo Vallecano.

articles.title: Luis Enrique explica por qué ha renovado con el PSG hasta 2030: "En París ha habido una conexión auténtica"
articles.standfirst: "París es diferente, París es especial. Existe la confianza del club, del presidente y de Luis Campos"
articles.summary: "París es diferente, París es especial. Existe la confianza del club, del presidente y de Luis Campos"
articles.body: Luis Enrique aprovecha la oficialización de la ampliación de su contrato con el PSG hasta 2030 para expresar su amor por París y por quienes integran el club. El PSG compartió una entrevista realizada a Luis Enrique, realizada antes del triunfo por 3-1 contra el Le Mans, para celebrar la renovación del entrenador español. Luis Enrique, que vive su cuarta temporada en el PSG, reconoce que "París es diferente, París es especial. Existe la confianza del club, del presidente y de Luis Campos (director deportivo)". "La conexión con Luis Campos fue muy especial desde los primeros días. Recuerdo una frase que pronuncié cuando dirigía a la selección española: 'No sé cuál será el resultado al cabo de varios años, pero sé que perderemos partidos. Quizás perdamos un encuentro, una clasificación para un Mundial o una Eurocopa jugando de esta manera. Pero estoy plenamente convencido de que esta forma de jugar es la mejor para ganar'. Normalmente, no siempre logro establecer esa conexión. En París ha surgido una conexión auténtica con la afición y con el club", subrayó. El ex del Barcelona, Real Madrid y Sporting destacó que "soy extranjero, pero espero seguir vinculado a esta ciudad el resto de mi vida". Luis Enrique recuerda que "ese fue nuestro primer objetivo al llegar al PSG: hacer historia. El deseo constante de ganar es una característica esencial de la élite. Quiero ganar el partido de pádel contra Achraf Hakimi, luego ganar el partido del día siguiente, ganar en el entrenamiento, ganar el próximo partido. El objetivo es siempre el mismo: ganar y seguir ganando. Me gustaría que se nos reconociera como un equipo respetuoso, valiente y ambicioso, formado por jugadores de gran talento. Creo que es importante mostrar a los niños que se puede jugar y ganar al fútbol disfrutando. También es necesario que los aficionados disfruten viéndonos jugar". "En los últimos dos o tres años, he conocido a personas que no tenían ningún vínculo especial con el club, pero que me decían que les gustaba el juego de nuestro equipo. Para mí, es un cumplido maravilloso. Es algo muy positivo que valoro enormemente", compartió. Luis Enrique, que suma 13 títulos oficiales con el PSG, cree que "sigo siendo el mismo, con los mismos errores. No soy perfecto y continúo cometiendo muchos. Intento mejorar cada día; tengo experiencia en el fútbol, pero eso no significa que crea tener siempre la razón o que no pueda seguir progresando. No quiero ser un entrenador que da órdenes constantemente y les dice a los jugadores: "Tienes que hacer esto, aquello y lo otro". Deben entender el esquema de juego para tomar la mejor decisión en cada momento. Esa es la clave. También deben ser capaces de proponer soluciones y gestionar las distintas situaciones que se presenten". Respecto a la gestión del equipo compartió que "no le corresponde únicamente al entrenador decidirlo todo. Avanzamos todos juntos y los jugadores deben asumir más responsabilidades. Anticipamos las situaciones que podríamos encontrar y cómo actuará el rival. Pero, durante el partido, son los propios jugadores quienes deben entender lo que sucede en el terreno de juego". "Para ser sincero, ¡me da un poco de miedo! La brecha de edad entre los jugadores jóvenes y yo aumenta cada año. Pero, al mirar atrás en mi carrera como entrenador, me doy cuenta de que siempre he logrado establecer buenas relaciones con los jugadores. Creo que eso puede continuar, incluso con esa diferencia de edad. Me gusta mucho reír, bromear y estar cerca de los jugadores. Es algo que me llena de energía: conectar con ellos, hacer bromas, compartir momentos juntos. Recuerdo que Vitinha a veces me dice: 'No sé si hablas en serio o no'. ¡Y yo le respondo que le toca a él interpretarlo! (risas). Cada jugador necesita un enfoque distinto según el momento. Algunos necesitan ánimo; otros, un mensaje más exigente. Intento encontrar la mejor manera de comunicarme con cada uno. Es apasionante, y eso es lo que me gusta de mi profesión. Todo evoluciona constantemente, al igual que nuestro equipo, que siempre está en movimiento", desveló. Luis Enrique huye de comparaciones con otros entrenadores: "Nunca me ha motivado la idea de compararme con otros entrenadores. Cada uno sigue su propio camino, y eso es algo que todo el mundo debería entender. Muchos entrenadores buscan copiar lo que les funciona a otros. Para mí, lo más importante es seguir tu propia trayectoria. Eso implica hacerse preguntas. ¿Es esta la forma en que quiero que juegue mi equipo? ¿Es esta la forma en que quiero que pierda, si es que tiene que perder? Probablemente sea una de las cosas más difíciles de aceptar para un entrenador. Pero son precisamente las derrotas las que nos obligan a cuestionarnos a nosotros mismos». "No necesito motivarme mirando a otros entrenadores. No tengo intención de intentar mejorar mi palmarés o mi currículum simplemente para superarlos. Estoy muy contento con lo que he logrado hasta ahora. Sigo teniendo la ambición de ganar muchos trofeos y de seguir ganando. Pero, cuando llegue el momento de perder, habrá que aceptarlo de la mejor manera posible. Habrá otro equipo, otro entrenador, otra familia, otro club que ganará y será feliz. Así es la vida", declaró en la entrevista difundida por el PSG.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: How much did their rule breaking cost your team?
articles.summary: The potential impact of Manchester City's rule breaking runs deep, including missed Champions League qualification, relegation and Premier League prize money.
articles.body:
Imagine a world where Manchester City had not used "sham contracts" to build a team capable of winning three Premier League titles, one FA Cup and three EFL Cups.

If City were the winners, then there had to be losers.

Not just those teams who finished runners-up or lost cup finals.

The potential impact runs much deeper and includes missed Champions League qualification, relegation and Premier League prize money.

Thirty-five other teams played in the English top flight between 2009 and 2018.

And every one could in some way claim to have been left financially out of pocket.

City, of course, continue to deny any wrongdoing and they have appealed. But as it stands they are guilty of all charges related to inflating their sponsorship income to the tune of £830m, plus another £90m in expenses.

Strip that money out and it changes the whole complexion of the competition.

BBC Sport has crunched the numbers to assess the potential financial impact on the top flight.

When Sheikh Mansour bought Manchester City in 2008 they were far removed from the club you see today.

Since finishing fifth in 1991-92, the last season before the formation of the Premier League, City's highest placing had been eighth in 2004-05.

The Abu Dhabi money poured in via what the Premier League's independent commission described as a "disguised funding scheme". It took the club's sponsorship revenues from being on a par with Stoke City in 2008-09 to eventually overtaking those of Manchester United .

City finished fifth in 2009-10. Since then, not once have they finished outside the top four in the Premier League.

Did this money deny other clubs a place in the competition, and other kinds of success?

Nor is it saying any one team would definitely have avoided relegation or reached the Champions League.

It is about chance, the possibility that a very different City team would have taken to the field without the hundreds of millions pumped in by the club's Abu Dhabi owners.

It has not considered potential future earnings from success, including sponsors' bonuses and further prize money.

Nor has it factored in players who may feel they have missed out on salary increases, or triggered payments, for how their club might have performed.

Missed potential Champions League earnings

What Manchester's 'super-profit' deal with City owners has paid out so far

Were any current Man City players signed during charges period?

How City gained £1.17bn, and others may have lost £844m

The full impact of City's behaviour on other clubs could be calculated at £844m.

£217.8m in missed Champions League prize money

£88.3m related to domestic cup competitions and the Europa League

We calculated these figures by taking published prize money from the relevant seasons.

For Premier League place money, each team that finished below City is considered to have potentially missed a payment for one place.

For relegation, this is the minimum value of being in the Premier League for the next season, minus the received parachute payment.

For the Champions League, we took City's earnings from the following seasons and deducted the impacted teams' Europa League prize money.

But City also earned prize money themselves during this period.

Across the competitions, City were paid £1.17bn:

£812.3m from the Premier League - total income from prize money and broadcast revenues

£300,000 from the three EFL Cup victories

The most impacted: How Spurs could have missed out on £120m

"We have lived through a period of deception," former Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino said last month.

"No type of punishment will make it possible to repair what was done."

You can see his point. Spurs finished one place outside the Champions League positions in four (although one only was under Pochettino) of the eight seasons in which City qualified for Europe's elite competition.

BBC Sport took City's earnings from the Champions League in the following season, and deducted Tottenham 's Europa League prize money.

Over the four seasons Spurs missed out, Manchester City earned £148.2m from the Champions League, with Tottenham taking £29.9m from the Europa League.

The 2014-15 campaign led to the biggest deficit, as City finished second in the Premier League and Tottenham came fifth. City received £71.2m for reaching the Champions League semi-finals in the following season, but Spurs were only paid £17.7m from the Europa League - a difference of £53.5m.

Spurs also finished behind City in the Premier League table six times, with the cumulative prize money difference worth £6.6m.

The north Londoners did benefit in the 2013-14 season, as they only qualified for Europe because City beat Sunderland in the final of the EFL Cup.

Spurs gained £5.1m from their 2014-15 Europa League campaign which would not have been possible without City's success.

Taking into account all competitions, that produced a net financial loss for Spurs of £119.9m.

Did City's EFL Cup win cost Liverpool £37.8m?

The 2015-16 EFL Cup final proved to be decisive for Liverpool 's hopes of European football.

Jurgen Klopp's men lost to City on penalties following a 1-1 draw. The Europa League place transferred to the league, and went to West Ham United.

Liverpool only finished eighth, which was not enough to qualify for Europe.

Had Liverpool won the final, they would have entered the Europa League, and this provides a key financial comparison.

Manchester United won the Europa League in 2016-17, receiving prize money of £37.8m. As part of that amount, the Red Devils' market pool payment, which is based upon the value of the television rights, was £26.6m.

While we cannot say for certain that Liverpool would have won the Europa League, they were a club of similar stature to Manchester United , which provides a comparison.

The market pool share may also have been slightly lower with both Liverpool and Manchester United involved.

Together with Premier League place money of £10.6m - Liverpool finished below City in all nine relevant seasons - the total financial impact on the Merseyside club was £52.3m.

As for the FA Cup, City won it just once in the period they were scrutinised over, beating Stoke in 2010-11. The difference in prize money was £900,000, with the runners-up going into the Europa League.

Everton missed out on the Champions League once, in 2013-14, and on four other occasions they finished one place below the final Europa League spot.

The Champions League place is calculated to be worth £32.6m - the £39m earned by Manchester City minus the Toffees' £6.4m winnings from the Europa League they competed in instead.

The combined impact on missing out on the Europa League four times is £23.2m.

Add on the £10.6m from Premier League prize money, and the total financial effect is £66.4m - making Everton the third-most impacted club.

Did two relegations cost Hull City £99m?

While parachute payments provide something of a cushion, relegation from the Premier League is still a considerable financial hit.

Could the teams who finished in 18th place, one spot from safety, argue that they might have stayed up but for City?

There are a couple of ways of looking at this.

Firstly, the results against City who took at least four points off every 18th-placed team other than Birmingham.

Secondly, the mere fact that City were able to assemble a squad far better than their finances should have allowed. Could they otherwise have been involved in relegation battles?

Again, this is not to say City would have been relegated. It is about chance.

BBC Sport has taken the total prize money earned by the team finishing in 20th in the following season. That suggests a minimum return for having stayed in the top flight.

Deducted from that is the first season of parachute payments to give a net amount.

Hull were relegated twice in the period, costing the Tigers £93.78m.

The Tigers finished below City in the table four times, adding £5.2m in place money to the sum.

It leaves the East Yorkshire club as the second-most impacted on £99m.

Swansea are fourth in the table with £63.1m. Of that total, £54m is from relegation and £9.1m in place money from the seven seasons the Swans were in the top flight.

Newcastle suffered relegation by finishing 18th in 2015-16, costing them a projected £60.4m, of which £7.9m was place money.

Norwich (£43.8m), Wigan (£39.6m), Burnley (£31.1m), Bolton (£26.4m) and Birmingham (£25.1m) also suffered relegations in 18th place.

Alongside Tottenham , four other teams missed out on Champions League football by one place across the eight seasons when City qualified.

The biggest impact was on Chelsea , who finished fifth in 2017-18.

City earned £79.2m from reaching the quarter-finals of the Champions League, with Chelsea getting £39.4m from winning the Europa League. That left Chelsea with a deficit of £39.8m.

Also just missing out on the Champions League were Everton (5th in 2013-14, £32.6m deficit), and Arsenal (5th in 2016-17, £22.1m deficit).

The only team not to experience much of a financial impact were Manchester United , who were fifth in 2015-16.

City got no further than the round of 16 in the Champions League, earning £42.6m, while United won the Europa League that season, receiving £37.8m. It left the Red Devils with a deficit of £4.8m.

In the Premier League there is no specific prize pot for being crowned champions.

Broadcast revenue is allocated on a merit basis by final league position.

It is a 1+1 system, so the club in 20th get the base payment. Then the team in 19th get the base payment two times. For 18th, it is that base amount three times, and so on.

It means that the only financial difference, in prize money at least, for the team finishing runners-up in one of Manchester City 's three title-winning seasons is one base payment.

Could any team claim they might have finished one place higher?

The value of a Premier League place rose sharply in line with the broadcast deals over the period of City's offences.

In 2010-11 it was £755,881 per place, and by 2016-17 it was up to £1.94m.

If any compensation were to be considered, Everton , Liverpool and Stoke City would have the biggest claim of £10.7m, having finished below City in all nine seasons.

West Brom and West Ham's total is £9.9m, with Swansea on £9.1m.

At the other end of the scale are the seven clubs who spent one season in the Premier League, including Blackpool (£756,756), Portsmouth (£800,424) and Huddersfield (£1.93m).

articles.title: Ronaldo scores, waves Saudi scarf in Al-Nassr’s win after security delay
articles.summary: Al-Nassr’s AFC Champions League game in Riyadh was delayed for one hour due to a security warning amid Houthi attacks.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo lapped up adulation in Al-Nassr’s Asian Champions League win at home, when the captain scored his team’s second goal and waved a Saudi scarf afterwards as a security threat caused a long delay in Riyadh.

The Saudi Pro League champions beat ⁠Uzbekistan’s Neftchi 3-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite at Al-Awwal Park on Monday, after a delayed start to the game in the capital due to a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthis.

Kick-off was delayed after Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence issued a safety warning 15 minutes before ⁠the scheduled start time in Riyadh, which has been targeted by missiles fired from the Houthis in recent days.

The crowd remained in their seats as the teams waited in their dressing rooms.

The Saudi-led coalition said it had twice intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles launched Monday by the Houthi rebels towards Riyadh. At least three explosions could be heard Monday night in the city.

Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence, which had warned residents through alerts sent to their phones, later said the danger had passed.

The Saudi Arabia-led coalition fighting in Yemen said its forces intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh, as the city reeled from attacks that have killed at least 14 people in recent days.

Residents of Riyadh reported several powerful explosions on Monday night, moments after a text message to their phones warned of an aerial threat.

The Houthis, who control Yemen’s most populous areas, including the capital, Sanaa, said their target in Riyadh had been King Khalid International Airport.

The renewed attacks came as King Khalid airport in Riyadh remains closed after a Houthi attack on Saturday that killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300. Another strike on Sunday killed one person and wounded 11.

Ange Postecoglou’s side shook off the interruption to go in front ⁠through Angelo in the 33rd minute with a deflected strike before Ronaldo doubled the lead nine minutes later.

The 41-year-old struck after Sadio Mane delivered a looping cross from the left that Aiman Yahya directed into Ronaldo’s path with his chest, and the Portuguese forward lashed the ‌ball into the bottom corner with a shot on the turn.

Alisher Odilov pulled one back for Neftchi six minutes into the second half, but Ikromjon Alibaev’s red card for a foul on Mohamed Simakan in the 65th minute and an own goal by Anvarjon Gofurov 13 minutes later sealed the win for Al-Nassr.

Following the win, Ronaldo and his teammates applauded the sparse home crowd behind Al-Nassr’s goal.

As he strolled around the goal, a supporter passed on a green Saudi neck scarf to Ronaldo, who waved it with one hand before draping it around his neck.

Meanwhile, defending champions Al-Ahli scored twice in the second half to pick up their first win of the new ⁠campaign as Marino Pusic’s side beat Al-Wasl from the United ⁠Arab Emirates 3-1.

Roger Ibanez put Al-Ahli ahead with a 20th-minute header, but Pedro Malheiro levelled in the third minute of first-half stoppage time.

Goals from Trincao and Feras Al-Brikan in the 58th and 91st minutes respectively ⁠moved Al-Ahli onto four points from their opening two matches.

“We created also in the first half, but in the second half we ⁠made our goals, and I think that was the ⁠difference,” said Trincao. “Physically we were a little bit better, and that was the key to changing the game.”

Houssine Rahimi scored twice as Al-Ain defeated Air Force Club 4-1 in Basra, while Hossein Goudarzi’s 60th-minute goal earned Iran’s ‌Esteghlal a 2-1 win over Al-Gharafa.

A last-minute penalty from Dostonbek Khamdamov salvaged a 1-1 draw for Pakhtakor against Brendan Rodgers’ Al-Qadsiah in Tashkent, while Tractor from Iran were ‌held ‌to a 0-0 draw by Qatar’s Al-Shamal.

The top eight finishers in the 16-team league phase in both East and West Asia will progress to the knockout rounds.

articles.title: Paul Pogba reclama desde su limbo vital el infierno para el Manchester City
articles.standfirst: "Sólo espero que esto no afecte a la Premier League. Ojalá podamos (el Manchester United) recuperar dos títulos"
articles.summary: "Sólo espero que esto no afecte a la Premier League. Ojalá podamos (el Manchester United) recuperar dos títulos"
articles.body: Paul Pogba sigue sopesando su próximo paso tras su sorprendente salida del Mónaco. El ex de Manchester United y Juventus habla desde su particular limbo futbolístico y exige que el Manchester City entregue los títulos de la Premier League tras ser declarado culpable de 114 cargos. "Para ser sincero, no tengo nada que decir... Pero sólo espero que esto no afecte a la Premier League. Ojalá podamos (el Manchester United) recuperar dos títulos", declaró el futbolista francés de 33 años en declaraciones que reproduce el 'Daily Mail' en los boxes del circuito urbano de Marina Bay durante el Gran Premio de Fórmula 1 en Singapur, reclamando para su United los títulos de la Premier de 2017-18 y 2020-21. Paul Pogba, que es agente libre, viajó a Singapur de la mano de su patrocinador adidas tras estar la semana pasada en París junto a su esposa Zulay en la gala 'The Business of Fashion 500'. Paul Pogba jugó con el Mónaco tras 808 días de suspensión, después de ser sancionado cuatro años por dar positivo por consumo de DHEA (Dehidroepiandrosterona). Tras disputar únicamente seis partidos en una temporada con el Mónaco, a cambio de un salario de 52.044 euros semanales, su contrato fue rescindido prematuramente. La prensa inglesa apunta a que el futuro futbolístico de Paul Pogba podría estar en la MLS de Estados Unidos. DC United, Inter Miami y New York City FC son los tres equipos de la MLS que podrían haber mostrado interés por el campeón del Mundial con Francia en 2018.

articles.title: El árbitro del Levante-Sevilla denunció el lanzamiento de "multitud" de botellas al campo
articles.standfirst: Sucedió durante uno de los goles que marcó Isaac Romero
articles.summary: Sucedió durante uno de los goles que marcó Isaac Romero
articles.body: El colegiado del Levante-Sevilla, disputado este pasado lunes en el Ciutat de València y que acabó con 3-3, reflejó en el acta el lanzamiento de "multitud botellas de plástico, vasos y otros objetos" durante la celebración del tercer gol del equipo andaluz en el minuto 95 del partido. Tal y como recoge en el acta del partido el árbitro Adrián Cordero Vega, en el minuto 95 tras la consecución del 2-3 "aficionados del club local identificados por el color de sus camisetas, lanzaron multitud de botellas de plástico, vasos y otros objetos a la zona de celebración del gol sin llegar a impactar ninguno de ellas". En ese momento, tal y como explicó en el acta el colegiado, aplicaron "el paso 1 del "Protocolo de lanzamientos y objetos", una vez dicho por megafonía se reanudó el partido sin llegar a producirse más incidente de este tipo". En algunas imágenes que se han difundido a través de las redes sociales sí se aprecia que al menos una botella impacta en el grupo de jugadores del Sevilla mientras celebran el gol y otra golpea en la pierna de Juan Iglesias tras caer primero en el suelo y rebotar en el futbolista del Sevilla. El lanzamiento de objetos al campo coincidió con la polémica celebración del futbolista del Sevilla Isaac Romero, que fue expulsado al ver la segunda amarilla por mandar callar a la afición del Levante, llevándose el dedo índice a la boca, una circunstancia que el árbitro explicó en el acta como una forma de dirigirse a la grada de "forma provocativa". Tras el encuentro, el entrenador del Sevilla, Luís García, explicó en la rueda de prensa que le habían golpeado con una botella en el tramo final del encuentro. "Hay que identificar a esa gente que tira una botella, aquí (en Valencia), en Sevilla o en cualquier campo", comentó. El partido, además, había estado marcado por los graves incidentes ocurridos durante el mediodía del lunes, cuando casi un centenar de ultras del Levante y del Sevilla participaron en una reyerta en la que se lanzaron botellas y sillas y en la que usaron palos para golpearse.

articles.standfirst: El problema muscular que sufrió ante Osasuna queda en nada y el brasileño podría jugar
articles.summary: El problema muscular que sufrió ante Osasuna queda en nada y el brasileño podría jugar
articles.body: La sesión de entrenamiento de este martes, última para el Betis antes de enfrentarse mañana al Oporto en La Cartuja en el partido de la segunda jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League, ha tenido una buena noticia para Manuel Pellegrini. El brasileño Antony ha comenzado la jornada de trabajo con sus compañeros y apunta a estar disponible para este primer partido del torneo continental con los verdiblancos como locales. Antony sufrió molestias musculares en los minutos finales del duelo ante Osasuna del pasado domingo. Las cámaras de Movistar LaLiga TV captaron incluso una conversación del futbolista con el Ingeniero, en la que le explicaba la zona donde había sentido el problema, y el gesto de preocupación del entrenador chileno. Ayer, el brasileño fue revisado por los médicos y se probó sobre el césped, en el entrenamiento a puerta cerrada. Y hoy se han confirmado sus buenas sensaciones. Así, salvo sorpresa, Antony estaría disponible para jugar mañana ante el conjunto portugués en un partido que significa el regreso de la Champions a Sevilla con el Betis como protagonista más de 20 años después. El resto de la plantilla, incluido Ruibal quien seguramente tenga que esperar unos días más para volver a las convocatorias, se ha ejercitado con normalidad, a excepción del lesionado Junior, única baja confirmada para mañana. Pellegrini comparecerá este mediodía, acompañado por Marc Bartra, en la rueda de prensa oficial previa al partido, desde la sala de prensa de la Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol. El Oporto, por su parte, no tendrá entrenamiento oficial en La Cartuja, pero sus jugadores sí estarán en el césped esta tarde, aprovechando la comparecencia ante los medios de comunicación de su técnico y de un jugador todavía por determinar por parte del club portugués.

articles.title: Laporta: "El Barça es el equipo que mejor fútbol juega de Europa"
articles.standfirst: El presidente culé atendió a los medios antes de ir a la comida de directivas en la isla de Galatasaray
articles.summary: El presidente culé atendió a los medios antes de ir a la comida de directivas en la isla de Galatasaray
articles.body: Joan Laporta atendió a los medios de comunicación en Estambul antes del partido de esta noche entre el Barcelona y el Galatasaray asegurando que el conjunto azulgrana "es el que mejor juega a fútbol de Europa". "Es un partido de la Liga de Campeones, la mejor competición de clubes del mundo, y llegamos en un buen momento. Ayer también tuvimos un entrenamiento aquí al que asistimos, y se notaba mucha intensidad; todos estaban muy motivados. Tenemos buenas sensaciones", dijo el máximo mandatario culé. Laporta también quiso hablar de Lamine: "Puede ganar el Balón de Oro, se lo merece". También valoró la buena racha del Barça, que podría ganar su décimo partido seguido. "Estamos ganando partidos, eso es lo que nos interesa, y en LaLiga sé que llevamos ocho, y ya es un récord", dijo. "La voluntad es que seamos candidatos a ganar todas las competiciones en las que participemos. Porque tenemos un equipo muy competitivo, porque tenemos un equipo muy bien remunerado, porque el trabajo realizado durante el verano fue excelente, Deco y su equipo hicieron un trabajo extraordinario. Tenemos una plantilla muy competitiva y la exigencia actual es alta, muy alta. Hemos empezado bien LaLiga y aquí estaremos para la Supercopa en febrero", comentó el presidente. "También tenemos la Copa y queremos ser candidatos a ganar la Champions League. Sabes que todos estamos muy ilusionados, no solo los jugadores, sino también los entrenadores, la comunidad deportiva, la directiva, todos, y todo el Barça. Así que, por supuesto, cuando ganemos, nos marcaremos ese objetivo", comentó. "Creo que estamos practicando el mejor fútbol de Europa y, por lo tanto, el mejor del mundo. Otros equipos que también lo están haciendo muy bien, como el PSG o el Bayern de Múnich, son candidatos a ganar las competiciones en las que participamos. Y siempre hay algún equipo que da la sorpresa, y hay que tenerlo en cuenta", dijo Laporta ilusionado. "Pero en cuanto a calidad futbolística, creo que, bueno, ahora mismo somos nosotros los que estamos jugando mejor. Y, además, jugamos mejor y damos espectáculo. Eso hace que los aficionados, y sobre todo, por supuesto, los seguidores, se lo pasen bien. Tenemos un juego divertido, me gusta", indicó el presidente. El mandatario no quiso entrar a valorar las polémicas en torno al Real Madrid y Vinicius: "No tengo nada que decir. Yo voy a hablar del Barça. Estamos aquí en Turquía para enfrentarnos al Galatasaray y ahora vamos a disfrutar de la comida oficial. Estambul es una ciudad fantástica. Para quienes no la conozcan, la recomiendo". En cuanto al rival de esta noche, fue claro: "El estadio es un infierno. Yo he estado aquí. Es uno de esos partidos que te gusta jugar porque hay mucho ambiente. Flick es quien mejor conoce al equipo. Si dice que ve ambición es porque ha tenido esa sensación, la valora en cada entrenamiento, la valora cuando está con su cuerpo técnico, con los jugadores. Y sí, él lo percibe todo". En cuanto a las opciones de ganar la Champions, Laporta fue claro: "Somos candidatos. Lo veo como un candidato y nos hemos fijado como uno de los objetivos para la Champions League este año". También valoró el buen ambiente en el equipo: "Creo que esa es la clave de todo: que haya espíritu de equipo y un buen ambiente en el vestuario. Creo que Flick lo ha logrado. La combinación con Deco está funcionando. Que exista este ambiente y esta ambición. Es porque, sea lo que sea que salga, lo hace muy bien".

articles.title: Tony Bloom: Hearts investor reiterates Scottish Premiership title ambition ahead of Celtic Park return
articles.summary: Hearts visit Celtic Park on Sunday for the first time since last season's Scottish Premiership title decider; Martin O'Neill's side won the league on the final day of the campaign after beating the Jambos; watch Celtic vs Hearts on Sunday from 2.30pm, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Brighton chairman completed a near £10m investment in the Tynecastle Park club last summer and instantly vowed to "disrupt the pattern of domination of Scottish football".

At their first attempt, Hearts - who are the only team in Scotland with access to Bloom's Jamestown Analytics network - missed out on a first top-flight title since 1960 on the final day of the season.

On Sunday, the two teams meet again at Celtic Park for the first time since that unforgettable title decider, live on Sky Sports .

"The way it [last season] ended, in difficult circumstances from a Hearts point of view, is exceptionally disappointing for the club and for me as well," Bloom told Sky Sports.

"At the end of the day, we've got to accept what's happened, if not be happy about how things ended."

When asked if he retains his view that Hearts will become the first non-Old Firm side to win the top-flight title since 1985, he added: "Absolutely. I'd be really disappointed if Hearts have not won the Scottish Premiership within the 10 years."

In the weeks and months that followed that defeat to Celtic, Hearts lost head coach Derek McInnes, captain Lawrence Shankland and midfielder Cammy Devlin to Rangers, while other key players like Alexandros Kyziridis and Alexander Schwolow also moved on.

However, using Bloom's Jamestown Analytics firm, Wouter Vrancken was appointed, and a number of new faces arrived, including the likes of Calvin Miller, Malachi Fagan-Walcott and Beau Reus.

A tough start to the season saw the club lose their Champions League and Europa League qualifiers, plus their Premiership opener to Aberdeen.

However, Hearts are now in the Conference League, the League Cup semi-finals and third in the top flight heading into Sunday's match, three points adrift of Rangers and two further back from Celtic.

Bloom said: "We move on to this season. We've started reasonably well, got a new head coach, so again we've got to be hopeful and optimistic for the season to come.

"It was really difficult with the head coach coming in literally just before the start of pre-season, but as a football club you have to recover, and you have to recover quickly. I think we have done.

"We've brought in a lot of new players, and there's a lot to play for in the season for Hearts, so I think there's a lot for the Hearts fans to look forward to this season."

Over a year ago, when Bloom told Sky Sports about his plans to topple the Old Firm, many did not take notice.

As the months went on and Hearts' title bid grew in momentum, it was not just Scottish football that stopped to take notice. The world did.

Until the 87th minute of that final game of the season, Hearts were set to become champions. In the end, they fell just short. However, their stock grew.

Despite a summer of change both in the dugout and to the squad, they are in the mix again this season. Yes, Bloom says he wants to end their 66-year wait for the title within a decade - but fans hope it will not take that long.

Bloom is chairman of Brighton, who also use his Jamestown Analytics firm. They have risen from England's League One to the Premier League, where they have finished in the top half in consecutive seasons, plus played in Europe.

Then there is Belgian club Union Saint-Gilloise, where Bloom became majority shareholder eight years ago. Through the same data-driven approach, they soon won the Belgian Cup and then claimed their first top-flight league title in 90 years.

Jamestown Analytics' involvement at Como of Italy is striking too. Over recent years, they have risen from the bottom of Italian football to the Serie A, where they finished fourth last season.

When Bloom believes in something, it normally happens. They split the Old Firm last season, and few would now bet against Hearts delivering the league title within his decade timeframe.

articles.title: 'Second round' entre Estados Unidos y España
articles.standfirst: Se espera una nueva batalla física, mental y futbolística tras la victoria de las nuestras el sábado
articles.summary: Se espera una nueva batalla física, mental y futbolística tras la victoria de las nuestras el sábado
articles.body: España y Estados Unidos volverán a verse las caras en la madrugada del martes al miércoles (1.00 hora española), apenas 74 horas de haberse enfrentado en Washington con triunfo español (0-2). En esta ocasión, las número 1 y 2 del ranking FIFA jugarán en el Subaru Park de Chester, un duelo en el que tanto Sonia Bermúdez como Emma Hayes podrán seguir haciendo probaturas de cara al Mundial de Brasil del próximo verano. La primera batalla, porque sobre el verde hubo más que fútbol, fue para España. “España ha evolucionado mucho a nivel físico en los últimos años. Recuerdo que, cuando yo jugaba, era un hándicap que teníamos que mejorar. Hoy en día la futbolista vive por y para el fútbol y ese es el camino que debemos seguir para que las nuevas generaciones mantengan este nivel”, valoró Sonia. “Queremos probarnos con las mejores selecciones y competir contra equipos con diferentes estilos. Sabemos que será muy complicado y distinto al del sábado en Washington”, añadió. A excepción de la portería, que todo apunta a que Misa será titular, el resto de internacionales sin minutos el sábado —véase Oihane, Alba y Lucía García— apuntan a tenerlos en Chester. “Queremos repartir minutos y probar estructuras”, valoró Sonia. La selección está disfrutando del gran sueño americano. Tras la victoria del sábado, el equipo desconectó visitando el Capitol One Arena para ver un partido de pretemporada entre los Washington Wizards y los Detroit Pistons. El domingo regresó al trabajo en el gimnasio y viajó a Filadelfia, donde ayer trabajó sobre el verde. La seleccionadora de Estados Unidos, Hayes, sabe que su equipo tendrá que dar más para poder ganar a la vigente campeona del mundo. “Cuando te enfrentas al mejor equipo del mundo, tienes que ejecutarlo todo a la perfección”, dijo. “Ya sabemos cómo juega España actualmente y conocemos la calidad que posee. Si les damos demasiado respeto en ciertas zonas del campo, nos castigarán”, añadió. “Debemos confiar en nuestras capacidades, especialmente en el último tercio, y ajustar los detalles necesarios para que el equipo ejecute lo que requiero. Afronto el partido con ilusión. Será otro gran enfrentamiento”, sentenció. Estados Unidos, campeón de cuatro Mundiales, siete medallas olímpicas o nueve torneos CONCAFAF entre otros hitos, no perdió un sólo partido como local en 24 años entre el 2000 y el 2024. Desde entonces, la selección de las barras y las estrellas ha cedido cinco veces como local. Cayó (0-2) ante México en la Copa Oro el 26 de febrero de 2024 en Carston; frente a Japón (1-2) en la She Believes Cup el 26 de febrero de 2025 en San Diego; ante Brasil (1-2) en un amistoso el 8 de abril de 2025 en San José; frente a Portugal (1-2) el 23 de octubre de 2025 en Chester; y la mencionada derrota ante España (0-2) en Washington el sábado. ¿Habrá otra más? Será la undécima ocasión —y el undécimo rival— en la que España se enfrenta a un mismo equipo con apenas unos días de diferencia. lo hizo ante Rusia (1995), Países Bajos (2008), Austria (2009), Escocia (2012), Nueva Zelanda (2015), China (2015), Dinamarca (2024), Portugal (2025), Suecia (2025) y Alemania (2025). España y Estados Unidos se han enfrentado hasta ahora en cinco ocasiones con tres triunfos americanos y dos europeos. “No hay mejor escenario ni mejor rival”, coinciden en ambos bandos. Que arranque el segundo round.

articles.title: 'I’m Portuguese, but I belong to Saudi Arabia': Ronaldo kisses Saudi emblem, celebrates with flag after 981st goal in Al-Nassr’s emphatic 3-1 win
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, the Al-Nassr captain, scored his 981st career goal in a 3-1 victory over Neftchi Fergana, celebrating with a Saudi flag and expressing his attachment to Saudi Arabia amidst regional tensions. His gesture comes as Portugal seeks to reconcile with the star forward following a dispute regarding his international future.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo had another goal to celebrate on Monday, but it was what he did with a Saudi Arabian flag after the final whistle that caught attention. The Al-Nassr captain kissed the country's emblem before kick-off, then draped a Saudi flag scarf over his shoulders as he joined supporters in celebration after a 3-1 victory over Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana. The gesture came amid heightened tensions in Riyadh and days after Portugal signalled its desire to welcome him back.Ronaldo's Saudi flag gesture comes amid regional tensionsRonaldo scored his 981st career goal in Al-Nassr's 3-1 win in the second round of the AFC Champions League Elite, but his connection with Saudi Arabia was visible even before the match began.Cameras captured the 41-year-old kissing the Saudi national emblem on his Al-Nassr shirt, featuring the palm tree and crossed swords. After the final whistle, he asked supporters for a scarf bearing the Saudi flag, draped it around his shoulders and joined the team's famous Viking clap celebration.Riyadh had been on high alert following deadly Houthi missile attacks on King Khalid International Airport over the weekend. Monday's match was delayed by an hour after a security alert was issued in the Saudi capital, before the teams eventually took to the pitch.Al-Nassr opened the scoring through Angelo Gabriel before Ronaldo struck in the 42nd minute. Neftchi Fergana pulled a goal back through Alisher Odilov early in the second half, but an own goal from defender Buyan Siger restored Al-Nassr's two-goal advantage and secured the victory.The club's official Arabic account subsequently shared a clip of Ronaldo wearing the Saudi colours alongside the message, “I am Portuguese, but I belong to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.”The words were not a new declaration, however, as Ronaldo originally made the statement in June 2025 during an interview with Al-Nassr's official media after extending his contract until 2027. The club's English-language account also shared a photograph of the celebration with the caption, “A piece of Saudi, carried close to the heart.”Portugal wants Ronaldo back after international disputeThe timing of Ronaldo's gesture is particularly interesting because his international future has recently become uncertain following his departure from Portugal's national team camp.Ronaldo left the squad in September after a dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus, later accusing the manager of breaking his word over his playing time. The Portuguese Football Federation subsequently opened disciplinary proceedings and imposed a provisional suspension while the case is investigated.However, federation president Pedro Proença publicly softened the situation on October 10, saying Portugal wanted their captain back for the November international window. Jesus has also indicated that Ronaldo would be welcome provided he remains fit, continues playing for Al-Nassr and wants to represent his country.Ronaldo had already returned to club action on October 9, scoring his 980th career goal in Al-Nassr's 3-0 win over Diriyah Club. His strike against Neftchi Fergana took that tally to 981, leaving him 19 goals short of the 1,000-goal milestone.The forward has also made clear that he remains willing to play for Portugal after serving any suspension, provided he is physically fit and continuing to score for his club. With the federation now expressing its desire for reconciliation, November could offer an opportunity for Ronaldo to resume international duty if the disciplinary process allows it.For now, his latest appearance was about more than another goal, as the Saudi flag gesture offered a reminder of the attachment he has publicly expressed towards the country he has called home since January 2023.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El empate ante el Atlético Madrileño dejó dudas tácticas en el equipo que asumió el técnico como errores suyos
articles.summary: El empate ante el Atlético Madrileño dejó dudas tácticas en el equipo que asumió el técnico como errores suyos
articles.body: Ibai Gómez sorprendió el pasado domingo durante el partido contra el Atlético Madrileño cuando en el descanso quitó a Óscar Ureña, uno de los mejores jugadores del Real Zaragoza, para dar entrada a un central como Hugo Barrachina. Un cambio defensivo para pasar a jugar con tres centrales que nadie entendió. Su decisión no fue la mejor, visto lo sucedido en el segunda parte, en el que el cuadro maño no defendió mejor y casi acabó perdiendo el encuentro. Al final se salvó un punto de forma milagrosa. Lejos de echar balones fuera, el técnico asumió su culpa con toda naturalidad, algo que hacía mucho que no se veía en el club blanquillo. El ejemplo más reciente fue cuando avisó que los jugadores podrían disfrutar unas horas por la noche de las Fiestas del Pilar, ya que ayer y hoy no entrenan: "Igual os los encontráis pero seguro que no veis al que se ha equivocado, que he sido yo", indicó. "Estoy jodido porque me he equivocado en el planteamiento que he hecho. Asumo la responsabilidad porque no ha sido el correcto. Les he acelerado demasiado. El equipo es el que saca adelante este punto por alma", señaló en sala de prensa con su cachirulo en la muñeca por las fiestas del Pilar. Desde su llegada, el vasco se ha ido ganando a su plantilla y afición por su humildad, trabajo, optimismo y cercanía. Demostrando que es un gran gestor de grupo, teniendo enchufados a todos sus futbolistas jueguen o no. Muy alejado del perfil de otros entrenadores que han pasado por Zaragoza en los últimos años de ingrato recuerdo. Desde la normalidad más absoluta y autocrítica cuando toca, Ibai ha devuelto la ilusión al zaragocismo. Los aragoneses mantienen el liderato de su grupo gracias al último empate y, a partir de mañana comenzarán a preparar el partido del domingo contra el Murcia, segundo clasificado. Eso sí, lo harán a puerta abierta en la Ciudad deportiva, ya que el club ha decidido seguir celebrando las Fiestas junto a su afición. La unión hace la fuerza.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Tony Bloom has faith in title ambition for Hearts
articles.summary: Investor Tony Bloom says he would be "really disappointed" if Hearts fail to win the Scottish Premiership by 2035.
articles.body:
Tony Bloom says he would be "really disappointed" if Hearts fail to win the Scottish Premiership by 2035.

The Brighton chairman vowed to "disrupt the pattern of domination which has been in place for far too long" when completing the purchase of a 29% stake in the Edinburgh club.

At the time, in June 2025, he also shared his ambition to achieve top spot within a decade.

Hearts came so close to a first title since 1960 last season, leading the league for 250 days before a dramatic final-day defeat at Celtic Park.

"The way it [last season] ended, in difficult circumstances from a Hearts point of view, is exceptionally disappointing for the club and for me as well," Bloom told Sky Sports.

"At the end of the day, we've got to accept what's happened, if not be happy about how things ended."

Celtic and Rangers have won every title since Aberdeen's 1985 success, but Bloom is confident Hearts are on track to break the Old Firm stranglehold.

"I'd be really disappointed if Hearts have not won the Scottish Premiership within the 10 years," he replied when reminded of his initial target.

Why Hearts' title tilt is unlikely to be a one-off

Having finished two points behind champions Celtic in May, there has been a huge overhaul in personnel at Tynecastle.

Head coach Derek McInnes left for Rangers, along with captain Lawrence Shankland and midfielder Cammy Devlin.

With Wouter Vrancken now in charge, Hearts remain unbeaten at home in the league for over a year and sit third behind the Old Firm duo.

"We've started reasonably well, so again we've got to be hopeful and optimistic for the season to come," added Bloom as Hearts prepare to visit Celtic on Sunday.

"It was really difficult with the head coach coming in literally just before the start of pre-season, but as a football club you have to recover, and you have to recover quickly. I think we have done.

"We've brought in a lot of new players, and there's a lot to play for in the season for Hearts, so I think there's a lot for the Hearts fans to look forward."

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 6
articles.summary: Superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, in both literal and metaphorical terms, is starting to run away from the competition.
articles.body:
Superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, in both literal and metaphorical terms, is starting to run away from the competition.

On the field, Ohio State's elite playmaker has practically been uncoverable. In the 2026 Heisman Trophy discussion, Smith has steadily become the clear favorite to take home the most prestigious individual award in college football.

But as Smith and OSU prepare for a showdown at Indiana, a few other contenders have a potential marquee moment ahead in Week 7.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss (+1300)

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+4000)

Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State (+5500)

Kenny Minchey, QB, Kentucky : Thanks to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins against South Carolina and LSU, Kentucky is now 5-1. That's enough to keep an eye on Minchey, who's thrown for 1,394 yards, 12 total touchdowns and just 1 interception. Oklahoma hosts UK in Week 7.

Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri : Similar story at Mizzou, where Simmons has guided the program to a 5-1 start. He had a quiet showing in the recent win against Texas A&M, yet sports a passing line of 1,434 yards and 14 touchdowns.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : Dating back to the upset of Oregon, Oklahoma State has ripped off four straight wins. Mestemaker threw for 304 yards and two scores in a triumph over UCF, adding a rushing score. Saturday's trip to Houston is essentially a fork in the road for Mestemaker's candidacy.

Jesse Legree, WR, Oregon State : You know whose stats are stunningly comparable to those of Jeremiah Smith? That would be Legree, a true freshman just balling out at the other OSU. He's pulled in 38 passes for 932 yards and 12 touchdowns. Can the 4-2 Beavers avoid more losses to truly get Legree in the hunt?

Jayden Maiava, QB, USC : Maiava quieted the White Out crowd at Penn State with his 301 yards and three scores in a 31-23 win. Entering an open weekend, Maiava is second nationally in both passing yards (2,045) and touchdowns (18). He lacks a signature game, but USC still has to play Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA.

Devon Dampier, QB, Utah : In a 41-24 victory over Kansas, Dampier passed for 238 yards, rushed for 71 more and totaled four touchdowns. Utah is 5-0 with a favorable trip to Colorado up next.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : Soon enough, the "undefeated team" bump may nudge Stockton into a ranked position. Plus, he's thrown for 1,298 yards with 14 touchdowns to two interceptions while rushing for 134 yards and a score. That production is just a tier below a few others for now, though.

Josh Hoover, QB, Indiana : Overall, not a great showing from Hoover at Nebraska. He only completed 12-of-22 attempts and didn't lead a touchdown drive through three quarters. Yet in the closing frame, Hoover connected with Nick Marsh for a pair of long scores to help IU survive 20-17. Entering the Ohio State clash, Hoover has totaled 1,406 yards and 18 touchdowns with zero turnovers for 6-0 IU.

Malachi Toney, WR, Miami : Toney is on the fringe of this category, but it felt unfair to drop him after an idle weekend. While he remains an electric talent, Toney's numbers—39 receptions for 604 yards and six touchdowns—could use a jolt. If he shreds Florida State on Saturday like he did last season, Toney will stay safely in the mix.

Julian Sayin, QB, Ohio State : When someone throws for 242 yards and four touchdowns but isn't the biggest story on offense, you know there's serious talent surrounding him. Perhaps a trip to Indiana will be Sayin's shining moment, although he certainly isn't complaining about having Smith on the outside.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss : Chambliss has thrown for 1,435 yards, 113 on the ground, and 16 total touchdowns, with six turnovers. Those are perfectly fine numbers on a 4-1 Ole Miss team. Starting in Week 7, however, the Rebels take on No. 13 Missouri, No. 7 Texas, Auburn, No. 1 Georgia and Oklahoma in consecutive weeks. It's make-or-break time for Chambliss and Ole Miss.

5. Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State

Stockton, Chambliss and Sayin are pounding on the top-five door. There are decent arguments for putting any of them in front of Kamario Taylor.

The glaring issue on his résumé is the 33-point smackdown Alabama laid on Mississippi State two weeks ago. Taylor didn't play terribly, but he still committed three turnovers in the 56-23 loss.

So, it was an ideal moment for an open weekend to reset.

Taylor is back on Saturday with a trip to LSU, followed by a home contest with Oklahoma and a game at Texas. He was an awesome September story, but the rest of October will show if Taylor has staying power in the Heisman race.

Russell, similarly, may be a bit lower in your ranking. Stockton and Chambliss, in particular, have logical cases to leapfrog Alabama's signal-caller.

But I'm not going to shred a first-year starter for struggles with Georgia.

To be clear, it wasn't a great showing. Russell mustered a 16-of-30 line in the 20-17 loss, passing for 185 yards and a touchdown, with 41 rushing yards and a fumble. He took a terrible sack in the fourth quarter that moved Bama out of field-goal range while trailing by three points, too.

Without a bounce-back performance at rival Tennessee this weekend, Russell will likely drop out of B/R's top five. Again, it's already a debatable spot anyway.

At the same time, Russell's stat line—1,824 total yards and 16 touchdowns for a 5-1 team, including two victories over current Top 25 teams—is impressive.

Notre Dame remains a clear favorite in its journey to BYU, but a prime-time showdown with an unbeaten team is CJ Carr's toughest challenge to date.

The second-year starter has done exactly what you'd expect from a top QB against modest competition. After throwing for 181 yards and three touchdowns as ND smoked Stanford, he's guided the Fighting Irish to a 6-0 record with 1,447 offensive yards and 19 total scores to one interception.

BYU's defense, on the other hand, has yielded just 5.5 yards per attempt—which is tied for fourth-best nationally.

Carr has an opportunity for a signature game in Week 7.

Following an open weekend, Darian Mensah will restart his Heisman pursuit with a game against Miami's bitter rival.

The 'Canes are set to host Florida State on Saturday night. Miami is a heavy favorite in the matchup because FSU's defense has surrendered 500-plus yards in losses to SMU, Alabama, and Louisville.

Miami should win handily. That result is most important.

Smith, though, has managed some clear separation in the award's hierarchy. Mensah, who's totaled 1,517 yards and 17 touchdowns with zero turnovers, can reinforce his candidacy with a comfortable win over FSU.

The challenge for Mensah—and, realistically, for anyone else—is that Smith has been spectacular and isn't short on spotlight games.

This weekend, it's a matchup at Indiana. Ohio State is idle in Week 8 but returns with a trip to USC, then hosts Oregon. Heck, even Northwestern is now ranked—and then Nebraska is still 5-1 and Michigan is a rivalry.

You want attention? Good luck landing more than this guy.

Smith tallied four catches for 93 yards and two touchdowns in the 45-16 blowout of Maryland, lifting his season marks to 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 scores. All three totals are second nationally.

Although he's not a lock to hoist the trophy, Smith is undoubtedly the midseason front-runner for the Heisman.

articles.title: Former Liverpool footballer will not be made bankrupt
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has settled an unpaid tax bill with His Majesty's Revenue and Customs.
articles.body:
Former Premier League footballer Jamie Carragher, 48, will not be made bankrupt after he settled an unpaid tax bill with HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC).

Judge Nicholas Briggs dismissed a bankruptcy petition issued in August against the ex-Liverpool defender at the Insolvency and Companies Court earlier.

Kevin Hassan, for HMRC, told the hearing in London that the debt has been paid, with no figure given in court. It was previously said to be in the region of £700,000 to £800,000.

Carragher, from Merseyside, spent his entire professional career with Liverpool and was part of the squad which won the Champions League in 2005.

He retired in 2013 after making 737 appearances for the club and has since become a pundit, appearing on Sky Sports and CBS Sports.

articles.title: El Borussia Dortmund renueva a Niko Kovac
articles.standfirst: El entrenador, que llegó en 2025, se compromete hasta 2029
articles.summary: El entrenador, que llegó en 2025, se compromete hasta 2029
articles.body: Niko Kovac y el Borussia Dortmund han renovado su compromiso. El exentrenador de Croacia, Eintracht Frankfurt, Bayern, Mónaco y Wolfsburgo ha ampliado su contrato hasta 2029. “Juntos, hemos impulsado un desarrollo claro y sentado bases importantes para el futuro. Tenemos una visión clara de cómo queremos jugar al fútbol, cómo queremos rendir como equipo y qué se necesita para alcanzar nuestros objetivos", ha asegurado el croata, que llegó al Signal Iduna Park en enero de 2025, con el equipo undécimo en la Bundesliga. "Fundamentalmente, no nos conformaremos con lo logrado, sino que trabajaremos cada día para mejorar. Vemos un gran potencial y estamos convencidos de que, juntos, con plena convicción y gran determinación, podemos lograr mucho más”, prosigue Kovac, que seguirá 'escoltado' por su hermano Robert, exjugador de Bayern, Leverkusen, Juventus y Borussia Dortmund, entre otros, y Filip Tapalovic. El Borussia Dortmund, que marcha colíder, celebra la renovación de Kovac, que viene de guiar al equipo a un cuarto puesto en la 2024-25 y a acabar segundo la temporada pasada. “Con Niko Kovac hemos avanzado mucho desde que asumió el cargo hace poco más de un año y medio. Ha desarrollado al equipo de forma constante y goza de una gran aceptación en nuestro club", ha señalado Lars Ricken, director general de Deportes. "Niko Kovac se identifica profundamente con el BVB y, por lo tanto, encaja a la perfección con nuestro club. La sintonía entre Niko, su cuerpo técnico y nuestra dirección deportiva es sumamente beneficiosa", remataca Carsten Cramer, director general. “Desde mi primer día aquí, se ha forjado una relación de confianza entre Niko y yo. Niko trabaja con suma meticulosidad y, gracias a su experiencia, transmite una tranquilidad que beneficia a nuestro equipo. Estamos en contacto casi a diario y trabajamos juntos para dar los siguientes pasos y alcanzar el éxito con el BVB”, prosigue Ole Book, director deportivo. Desde su llegada en enero de 2025, Niko Kovac presenta un balance de 49 victorias, 14 empates y 17 derrotas en los 80 partidos que ha disputado. En el apartado anotador, suma 171 goles a favor y 98 en contra.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president received payment of £1.3m from World Cup company
articles.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been under pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in FIFA tournaments to private investors; he has confirmed he will stand for re-election in March 2027 as planned; financial documents reveal Infantino received undisclosed payments
articles.body:
FIFA has committed to publishing Infantino's salary, bonus and allowances in its annual report every year since 2016.

For 2024, he reported £3.88m ($5.1m) in salary but US tax filings show he also received £1.3m ($1.76m) from FWC2026, the company set up to organise and run this summer's World Cup, which was not publicly disclosed by FIFA in the annual report.

Article 43, paragraph 13 of FIFA's statutes reads: "The individual compensation of the FIFA president, the members of the council and the FIFA secretary general shall be made public."

When asked for comment, a FIFA spokesperson said: "FIFA does not pay a second salary to the FIFA president and complies with all reporting requirements in relation to compensation. The FIFA president's annual compensation, as well as other contractual benefits, are decided by the independent compensation sub-committee.

"FIFA strongly rejects any claims that it has failed to disclose any financial information and has violated FIFA's statutes. FIFA accounts are independently audited, and all declarations are in line with tax regulations in Switzerland, the United States and elsewhere.

"FIFA is fully focused on the FIFA Council meeting on Thursday and looks forward to discussions with its members to further grow the game following the most successful FIFA World Cup in history."

FIFA's secretary general Mattias Grafstrom received no extra payment from FWC2026, and neither did CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani, even though he chaired the FWC2026 board.

The US Internal Revenue Service filing which includes details of Infantino's undeclared second 2024 salary was first reported by The Times .

On Thursday, Infantino will meet the other 36 members of the FIFA Council in Zurich for the first time since he tried to part-privatise FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup, behind their backs.

Infantino's presidency has become mired in scandal and controversy, but he is refusing to resign despite losing the support of UEFA and some federations in North America and Asia.

He believes he has enough support to be re-elected in March next year, especially in Africa and South America.

No challenger who has a chance of beating him has emerged so far. Former Tottenham and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega wants to stand but he is unlikely to receive the backing of the five federations he needs to become an official candidate. Candidates have until November 18 to declare their intention to stand.

Infantino has been re-elected unopposed in the past two elections - in 2019 and 2023 - since he beat four other candidates to become president in 2016.

FIFA presidents are not allowed to remain in post for more than three terms, but Infantino is being allowed to stand again because FIFA is claiming his initial three-year term - from 2016 to 2019 - does not count towards their three-term limit.

articles.title: El Club 'Divertido' Lugo se lo pasa en grande: líder, invicto y mejor equipo de Primera RFEF
articles.standfirst: Los gallegos han sumado 19 puntos de 21 posibles y ayer le arrebataron el primer puesto a la UD Logroñés
articles.summary: Los gallegos han sumado 19 puntos de 21 posibles y ayer le arrebataron el primer puesto a la UD Logroñés
articles.body: Lugo sigue de celebración. Las Fiestas de San Froilán llegaron a su fin, pero su equipo de fútbol se ha colocado en lo más alto de la clasificación. Y el de baloncesto, el Breogán, ha hecho pleno de victorias en el arranque de la Liga Endesa (junto al Baskonia y el Real Madrid es el único que lo ha conseguido) con récord incluido: es el primer equipo en 41 años que supera los 100 puntos en las tres primeras jornadas. Pero volvamos al fútbol. En 2023, el Lugo cayó a Primera Federación tras 11 años asentado en el fútbol profesional. Muchos pensaron que volvería a la división de plata por la vía rápida, pero en las tres últimas temporadas ni siquiera llegó a disputar los playoffs: 10º en la 2023-24, 13º en la 2024-25 y 9º en la 2025-26. Ayer, tras derrotar 3-1 a la UD Logroñés, arrebató el liderato a los riojanos y se convirtió en el equipo más en forma de la categoría: es el que más puntos ha sumado, es el único invicto y es el que menos goles ha encajado. Ha ganado seis de sus siete partidos y sólo cedió un empate en Ponferrada, donde mereció más. Y hay motivos para ser optimista. Con su 19/21 iguala el mejor arranque en la historia de Primera Federación. Antes lo lograron el Castellón, el Tenerife, el Villarreal B, el Racing Ferrol, la Cultural y el Linares. Y todos, a excepción de los jienenses, acabaron logrando el ascenso a final de curso. Al frente del equipo está Borja Fernández, que sigue dando pasos de gigante como entrenador. El ex jugador de Real Madrid y Real Valladolid, entre otros muchos equipos, logró dos ascensos seguidos (de Tercera RFEF a Primera RFEF) con la UD Ourense, el equipo de su ciudad, antes de firmar por el Lugo este verano. El míster afirma que están "a un nivel muy alto desde el primer día" y que "lo que hay que hacer es seguir trabajando y no creernos que somos los reyes del mambo". Esto acaba de comenzar, pero el Lugo es una piña, un equipo muy sólido. Sólo ha estado una vez por debajo en el marcador y ha ganado dos partidos en el tiempo añadido. Y nadie, de momento, se ha llevado puntos del Anxo Carro, un estadio que ayer registró una entrada superior a los 3.500 espectadores... cifra poco habitual en la ribera del Miño. A pesar de los números y de las sensaciones, Borja tiene claro que hay que mantener los pies en el suelo porque, como reza el lema del club, Esto es Lugo y aquí hay que sachar. Hasta el final.
