articles.title: OFFSIDE: Why Ronaldo vs Messi is now less a debate and more a tragicomedy
articles.summary: Explore the evolving narratives surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi as their legendary rivalry transitions into a tragicomedy reflecting their late-career journeys. Delve into the decline of their international careers and the haunting echoes of their past magnificence.
articles.body: Hello and welcome to another edition of Offside.The most sublime TV shows often spiral into mediocrity. Game of Thrones was very hard to care about after Season 5, when they ran out of George RR Martin’s books and had to come up with something on their own, which was AI slop even before generative AI had hit our lives. House MD went downhill the moment they started focussing more on the Doc’s drug issues than the actual medicine. The same goes for Mad Men, where Don Draper’s personal issues became an albatross around a great show’s neck. And the same happened with The Boys, which began as an apt satire of our superhero-obsessed culture before becoming so bad in subsequent seasons that only Homelander’s narcissism – which started to resemble that of another man with blonde/orange hair who thinks he’s omnipotent – and Billy Butcher’s cussing kept the show from becoming completely banal. By the last season, it was running on fumes, and there was only one scene that made it worth watching all of them: Homelander losing his powers and getting tea-bagged by Butcher.It was worth the wait to see the world’s most powerful creature with a God complex being reduced to a mere mortal, more so since he had just killed Frenchie. And oddly, that final battle is starting to resemble the late-stage international careers of Lionel Messi and Ronaldo. And to put a cherry on the comparison, late-stage Ronaldo is starting to look even more like Homelander.Jeffrey Archer – a novelist known as much for his lifelong mendacity as his ability to pen compelling stories – had a format he first introduced with Kane and Abel and perfected over the years. In this format, he would take two contrasting Archer-types (pun intended) and run the rule over their entire lives from birth to death.Now, if he were to write about Messi and Ronaldo, he would probably begin with their lives. One, a tiny kid born in a middle-class neighbourhood in Rosario to the manager of a steel manufacturing plant and his wife, who worked in a magnet manufacturing plant.The other, a boy born into considerably more modest circumstances on the Portuguese island of Madeira, whose father worked as a municipal gardener and kit man at a local football club, named him not after the Brazilian footballer of the same name but after Ronald Reagan.Both would leave their homes soon. Messi, whose growth hormone deficiency threatened to derail any career in sports, finally signed a contract with Barcelona – famously signed on tissue paper – while Ronaldo joined Sporting’s academy in Lisbon, eventually attracting the attention of a Scotsman who knew a thing or two about forging youngsters into world-beaters.After torturing United’s stalwarts in a friendly – this was a time when they were Premier League beaters and not a banter club – the aforementioned Scotsman refused to leave the Sporting ground till they signed him. Ronaldo spent six years in Manchester, where his insouciant petulance was kicked out of him – sometimes literally – by Messrs Keane, Scholes and other members of the United first team, resulting in three Premier League titles, the Champions League and his first Ballon d’Or.Meanwhile, Messi progressed through La Masia to Barcelona’s first team, learning at the feet of Ronaldinho before Pep Guardiola pulled off football’s greatest switcheroo by moving him to a false nine role. He slowly became the footballer who looked like he had a button that allowed him to go into bullet-time mode.Messi’s and Ronaldo’s destinies – like football’s Karna and Arjuna’s – were always intertwined, and the Argentine got the first laugh when Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona beat Manchester United 2-0 in a match where the Blaugrana made the Red Devils look like a Sunday league team. The cherry on top for Messi fans was the fact that at a time when Ronaldo was known for his aerial prowess, it was the 5’7” magician who scored a header.Ronaldo would eventually move to Madrid in 2009 for a then-world-record £80 million, bringing the two men into direct conflict in what would become football's greatest individual rivalry, consuming everything like a supernova. Between them, they broke every scoring record, shared every Ballon d’Or, and the only meaningful interruption to their rivalry came when someone had to collect the trophy from the podium and hand it to one of them.But all great stories have to end, with Ronaldo moving to Juventus, returning to United and then leaving for Saudi Arabia after an almighty fit.Messi, leaving a debt-riddled Barcelona, went to PSG, where even the Neymar-Messi-Mbappé troika failed to recreate the magic before settling in Miami in Mammon’s, sorry, David Beckham’s warm embrace.Their international careers, however, had different trajectories, with Messi failing to replicate his club form for his country, a Maradona-esque burden that seemed to hang heavy over him, with every failure treated as evidence that he wasn’t as great as his coke-loving predecessor. He even announced his retirement in 2016 before eventually winning the Copa América in 2021 and leading Argentina to the World Cup in Qatar in 2022.The 2026 World Cup ended in heartbreak, but Messi was never a burden for his team, and it appeared that the rest of the Argentina team would run through a brick wall for Messi, and perhaps if they had bothered to play a little football too, the final result could have been different. Messi signed off with one final match after his father and manager passed away.Ronaldo, on the other hand, won Euro 2016 with Portugal, though during the final he was off the pitch with an injury, and two UEFA Nations League titles. During the World Cup, it actively felt like Ronaldo was becoming a burden on his Portuguese teammates. Throughout his career, Ronaldo’s sphere of influence had decreased, first from the entire pitch to a small area in the penalty box, and even that skillset appeared to desert him in his final days.And yet Ronaldo appeared to persist with his national team, showing the sort of insouciance that was associated with a pre-Ferguson Ronaldo before storming off after a disagreement.And then, in an extraordinarily long Instagram post of nearly 2,000 words that could masquerade as an Offside column, Ronaldo wrote the sort of explainer that SEO guys dream about and released it hours before Messi’s final farewell.The 11-slide Instagram manifesto began with a revelation that Ronaldo had prepared his retirement letter after the 2026 World Cup, but the 41-year-old claimed he was persuaded to stay and that the board had consulted him before appointing Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo also invoked Simão Coutinho, Al-Nassr’s sporting director, pointing out that Jesus, in a previous avatar, had reported to Coutinho. That felt oddly like the Portuguese version of the Delhi saying: “Tu jaanta hai mera baap kaun hai?”In every single way, it was reminiscent of late-stage Homelander becoming more and more convinced of his own immortality and becoming increasingly unhinged before meeting his fate at Billy Butcher’s hands.There was a time when the Messi vs Ronaldo GOAT debate had an inkling of merit.At that time, when Ronaldo said he was the “best in the world”, the world might have disagreed with him, but the way he went toe-to-toe with Messi suggested there was some merit to the debate. But in recent years, it feels more like a hollow chant, one that doesn’t convince anyone except Piers Morgan or iShowSpeed.Many years ago, Sir Alex Ferguson’s firm hand had forged Ronaldo’s career, turning a gifted teenager into a world-beater. In the late stages of his career, it’s quite clear there’s no Ferguson-like figure to lend him a shoulder, or perhaps Ronaldo has become a person who no longer listens to anyone else. Either way, it’s sad for anyone who has followed his career with interest to see what has become of the teenager of touch and tease who first made his Manchester United debut against Bolton and blew everyone away with his skills.And if Jeffrey Archer were to write the final chapter of these two intertwined lives, he would probably relish the irony that the boy from Rosario, who needed help to grow, eventually learnt when to say goodbye, while the boy from Madeira, whom Ferguson taught to grow up, appears unable to do the same. Homelander had to lose his powers before realising that he was a mere mortal. Ronaldo, thankfully, still has time to write a different ending. After all, the greatest tragedy would be for a man who spent his entire career defying the limits of human ability to be remembered for his inability to accept them.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Stroppa, cuarto técnico que cae en el 'calcio'
articles.standfirst: El Venezia, colista, ha perdido los seis partidos que ha disputado en su regreso a la Serie A
articles.summary: El Venezia, colista, ha perdido los seis partidos que ha disputado en su regreso a la Serie A
articles.body: El Venezia ha destituido a Giovanni Stroppa como entrenador después del mal arranque liguero, en el que el conjunto 'arancioneroverdi' ha perdido todos los partidos tras su regreso a la Serie A. "Bajo su dirección técnica, el club logró el ascenso a la Serie A en la temporada 2025-26, tras completar una destacada campaña en la Serie B", informa el club del norte de Italia en un comunicado. "El club 'arancioneroverde' desea agradecer a Giovanni Stroppa y a su cuerpo técnico el trabajo realizado, así como la profesionalidad, la dedicación y el compromiso demostrados durante su etapa en el Venezia FC", agregó. Stroppa deja así el club al que llegó en la temporada 2025-2026 y en el que logró la promoción del equipo a la primera categoría tras su primer año en la entidad de la ciudad del León de San Marcos. El Venezia ha perdido todos los partidos disputados esta temporada excepto uno, la primera fase eliminatoria de la Copa Italia en la que venció al Módena por 3-2. Posteriormente, en esta misma competición, cayó ante el Udinese. En Liga es colista. No ha conseguido ningún punto. Ha sido derrotado por el Lecce, la Fiorentina y la Lazio en casa y por el Milan, el Frosinone y el Atalanta a domicilio. Stroppa se convierte, de este modo, en el cuarto entrenador destituido en lo que va de temporada en Serie A. Cabe recordar que Paolo Valoni sustituyó a Fabio Grosso en la Fiorentina, Alberto Gilardino ocupó el lugar del español Carlos Cuesta en el Parma y Raffaele Palladino ocupó el puesto de Domenico Tedesco en el Bolonia.

articles.title: A Premier League giant to fall? Hull, Ipswich and Coventry are changing the relegation equation this season
articles.summary: Hull City, Ipswich Town and Coventry City are all clear of the Premier League relegation zone after six games; does this put a supposedly safe mid-table club or a big-name team in genuine danger of relegation to the Championship this season?
articles.body:
The Premier League's newly-promoted sides have often struggled to bridge the gap, with two consecutive seasons in 2023/24 and 2024/25 seeing all three newcomers relegated before Leeds and Sunderland helped buck that trend last season.

The lesson teams are learning is that survival is possible when a promoted team gets their recruitment, organisation and mentality right.

Hull and Ipswich already have nine points, while Coventry, following their 4-1 hammering of Newcastle, are on six.

No newly-promoted Premier League club since 1995/96 with at least 10 points after their first six games has subsequently been relegated (nine teams reached that points haul). The last nine newly-promoted teams to get nine or more points from their first six matches have all survived, which bodes well for Hull and Ipswich.

Coventry's emphatic victory over Newcastle on Monday night was particularly significant. Frank Lampard's side had started the campaign with four defeats and no goals, but two consecutive victories have transformed the mood around the club.

Ipswich, meanwhile, have shown the sort of resilience that can make the difference over a 38-game season, snatching a dramatic late win against Fulham. Hull have also put together a surprising run of results, showing they can compete and collect points against established top-flight opposition.

Three promoted clubs staying up would mean three other sides have to take their place, of course, potentially putting a supposedly safe mid-table club or a big-name team in genuine danger.

Hull, Ipswich and Coventry are outside the relegation zone and the early evidence suggests this is not simply a case of one promoted side riding a wave of momentum.

There is a collective challenge to the established order developing here.

Fulham, Tottenham and Bournemouth fill the bottom three spots at the minute and are winless after six games, while, like Bournemouth, Sunderland have a European campaign to negotiate and only have a win over Fulham on the board this season.

Aston Villa and Newcastle are going through big transition seasons and the bookmakers have Manchester City as third favourites for relegation with the possibility of a points deduction on the table following the independent commission finding them in breach of the Premier League's financial rules - City have denied wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal.

The danger is that poor form and the increased workload from potential European commitments can quickly become a crisis when confidence drains away and the pressure starts to build. The early relegation picture already suggests some established sides have reason to be concerned.

With Hull, Coventry and Ipswich refusing to follow the script, nobody should assume the three pre-season favourites for the drop are going down.

The relegation equation has certainly changed.

articles.title: Bartra: "¿Mi futuro? Estoy centrado en el presente y en rendir, esa es una pregunta para el club"
articles.standfirst: El central catalán termina contrato en junio y afronta mañana un nuevo partido de Champions
articles.summary: El central catalán termina contrato en junio y afronta mañana un nuevo partido de Champions
articles.body: Marc Bartra, uno de los capitanes de la primera plantilla del Betis, ha sido el encargado de acompañar a Manuel Pellegrini en la rueda de prensa oficial previa al partido de la segunda jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions que los verdiblancos disputan mañana en La Cartuja frente al Oporto. El central catalán ha hablado de ambición, confianza y compromiso, pero también de prudencia a la hora de afrontar este encuentro. Su mejor momento en el club: "Llevamos muchísimos años haciendo las cosas muy bien, creciendo año a año. A nivel de equipo, tener a muchos compitiendo juntos durante estos años, más la gente que ha venido a reforzarnos, hace que estemos a un gran nivel. Se está dando un momento muy bueno a nivel de juego; nos conocemos mucho y sabemos lo que quiere el míster tanto con balón como sin balón. A nivel personal me siento con mucha plenitud. Es un gran momento que hay que saborear, pero sobre todo hay que enfocarse en seguir a un gran nivel". Qué puede aportar en la Champions: "Lo que puedo aportar es lo que llevo haciendo durante todos estos años: sabiendo lo que quiere el míster de mí, lo que necesita el equipo, y estar al servicio del grupo a nivel defensivo, seguro y con confianza atrás. En una competición así, a nivel emocional es importante mantenerse con carácter y buena mentalidad porque en Europa cualquier detalle suma mucho. La concentración continua y liderar desde atrás es fundamental para que el equipo esté como tiene que estar". Jugar en casa con el Betis la Champions: "Es un privilegio total jugar la Champions. He tenido la suerte de hacerlo con el Barça y con el Borussia Dortmund, pero hacerlo con el Betis después de tantos años de crecimiento hace que tenga un sentimiento de pertenencia muy bueno y que sea más especial aún. Llevarlo a un grado de responsabilidad de jugar Champions es un privilegio que me encanta, y vivirlo ahora con esta plenitud es algo muy bonito". Cómo transmiten tranquilidad a los jóvenes: "De cara a los jóvenes o a los que tienen menos experiencia, el mejor ejemplo que podemos dar los veteranos es hacer lo que nos toca hacer en cada momento. Eso les da tranquilidad para que se suelten, porque son jugadores que están mostrando muchísimo nivel y deben seguir con esa dinámica". Tranquilidad tras la victoria en Lille: "Recuerdo una experiencia con el Borussia Dortmund donde recibimos un golpe, pero ahí se vio al equipo dar un paso adelante y no venirse abajo. Contra el Lille el equipo dio la cara y eso da la tranquilidad de que estamos en el camino correcto. Esa fuerza y esa unidad del grupo, sumadas al esfuerzo y al sentimiento de pertenencia, son muy importantes para seguir adelante". Qué siente jugando el torneo con el Betis: "Es un privilegio muy grande porque sabemos de dónde venimos: cuando llegué, el club hacía tres o cuatro años que había estado en Segunda división. Cada año fuimos creciendo hasta la llegada del míster, que nos inyectó esa mentalidad ganadora y la tranquilidad en momentos complicados. Sentimos que en la Champions y arriba en la Liga es donde nos gusta estar, pero siempre con los pies en el suelo y sin confiarnos". Jugadores peligrosos del Oporto: "El Oporto es un equipo que con balón está acostumbrado a atacar, no solo con buena salida de balón sino con jugadores desequilibrantes y de mucha calidad arriba. No quiero destacar a ninguno en particular porque tienen buenas individualidades, pero a nivel grupal nos va a exigir nuestra mejor versión tanto con balón como sin balón". Más años en el Betis: "Es una pregunta más para el club que para mí, porque estoy muy centrado en el presente, en rendir y en servir al equipo. Lo demás, que sea lo que Dios quiera". Qué significa Pellegrini en su carrera: "He tenido la suerte de tener a los mejores entrenadores del mundo y el míster es uno de ellos. Me ha hecho crecer a nivel de mentalidad, en lo que debo aportar en el campo y en transmitir esa seguridad y liderazgo. Es el entrenador con el que más he estado y soy de los jugadores con los que él más ha contado en su carrera, lo que me llena de orgullo y gratitud". Evitar exceso de confianza: "Todas las experiencias pasadas a nivel europeo sirven como aprendizaje y crecimiento. Cuando hemos atravesado momentos complicados, hemos respondido con una madurez muy importante, uniéndonos más como grupo. Estoy tranquilo en ese aspecto porque sabemos afrontar situaciones difíciles manteniéndonos fuertes como colectivo". Qué transmite Pellegrini: "Nos lidera no solo con palabras, sino con hechos. Le seguimos por su manera de hacer las cosas tras tantos años en la élite. Aporta una tranquilidad clave para no venirse arriba en las victorias ni hundirse cuando no se gana, centrándonos siempre en el presente". Jugar en casa la Champions y estado físico de Antony: "Es muy importante jugar en casa en Europa con el apoyo y el ánimo de nuestra afición. En cuanto a Antony, se le ve bien y ya veremos mañana a qué nivel está o si juega, lo cual dependerá del míster". Recuerdos de la última Champions del Betis: "Tenía 14 años cuando el Betis jugó Champions y lo recuerdo bien porque siempre me ha gustado mucho el fútbol. Para muchos niños y aficionados es la primera vez que verán al Betis en Champions; es un privilegio y trabajaremos para darles las máximas alegrías posibles". Su estado tras las molestias ante el Deportivo: "Fueron unas molestias por las que paré pronto para que no fuera a más. Me encuentro bien, con garantías de competir, estar a disposición y hacer un buen partido".

articles.title: Álex Sola regresa al grupo tras cumplir una semana de sanción disciplinaria
articles.standfirst: El extremo vuelve a entrenarse con normalidad después del castigo impuesto por el Almería tras su accidente de tráfico y dar más del triple de la tasa de alcohol permitida
articles.summary: El extremo vuelve a entrenarse con normalidad después del castigo impuesto por el Almería tras su accidente de tráfico y dar más del triple de la tasa de alcohol permitida
articles.body: Álex Sola ya vuelve a ser uno más en la UD Almería. El extremo donostiarra se reincorporó este lunes a los entrenamientos con el resto de sus compañeros después de permanecer una semana apartado de la dinámica del primer equipo como consecuencia del expediente disciplinario que le abrió el club. La entidad rojiblanca había decidido imponer una sanción deportiva y económica al futbolista tras el grave incidente protagonizado hace algo más de una semana, cuando estrelló su vehículo contra varios coches estacionados en la capital almeriense y, posteriormente, dio una tasa de alcohol de 0,76 miligramos por litro de aire espirado, más del triple del límite permitido para conducir. Tras varios días ejercitándose al margen del grupo y no entrar en la convocatoria del último encuentro ante el Leganés, el jugador volvió este pasado lunes a trabajar con normalidad a las órdenes de García Pimienta, poniendo fin al castigo deportivo impuesto por el club. De esta forma, recupera la condición de disponible para entrar en las convocatorias, aunque será el técnico quien decida cuándo vuelve a tener minutos de competición. Con esta reincorporación, el Almería da por cerrado un episodio que generó una gran repercusión y con el que quiso lanzar un mensaje de firmeza ante una conducta considerada incompatible con los valores que pretende transmitir la entidad, aunque una parte de la afición indálica cree que el castigo se ha quedado corto.

articles.title: Tres detenidos y treinta identificados: El parte de la pelea entre ultras del Sevilla y Levante
articles.standfirst: Ante los altercados, el cuadro granota solicitó un refuerzo policial en las horas previas al partido
articles.summary: Ante los altercados, el cuadro granota solicitó un refuerzo policial en las horas previas al partido
articles.body: Los tristes altercados que se produjeron este pasado lunes al mediodía, entre aficionados radicales entre el Sevilla FC y el Levante Unión Deportiva, se ha saldado con un total de tres detenidos y una treintena de personas identificadas por la policía antes del envite, según ha informado el Levante EMV. La pelea, que se produjo en la Avenida Santiago Rusiñol y en los aledaños del propio estadio Ciutat de Valencia, fue movilizada por agentes que se desplazaron hasta el lugar de los hechos donde detuvieron a estos tres individuos pertenecientes al grupo ultra sevillista "Biris". Los dos bandos que se enfrentaron, utilizaron sillas, de un local habitual en las previas de los partidos, material pirotécnico y bates, entre otros, y en los que provocaron diferentes destrozos en el mobiliario urbano. Ante esta situación, la entidad del barrio de Orriols solicitó un refuerzo policial de cara a las horas previas y durante el choque, en el que no se produjeron más altercados en el exterior, a pesar de los constantes lanzamiento de objetivos en las gradas del estadio entre los aficionados de los dos equipos.

articles.title: La Champions como oasis
articles.standfirst: El Madrid vuelve a Europa, un entorno que en Valdebebas se considera más amable, lejos del estrés semanal de la Liga
articles.summary: El Madrid vuelve a Europa, un entorno que en Valdebebas se considera más amable, lejos del estrés semanal de la Liga
articles.body: El Real Madrid vuelve este miércoles a una Champions League que, en este arranque, habla italiano para el club blanco. Tras el estreno ante el Inter de Milan, hace más de un mes, visita en esta ocasión a la Roma. Dos clubes en los que trabajó José Mourinho, hoy técnico blanco y portavoz, por acción u omisión, del hartazgo del club en las competiciones nacionales. El úlitmo episodio tuvo lugar el pasado sábado, con la famosa acción del gol anulado a Vinicius por un tirón de pelo a Saliba en el arranque de la jugada. Más allá de esa jugada en concreto, que en el club aceptan aunque con matices, se trata de la tensión que presidió todo el duelo. La actuación arbitral encendió a la grada, que cantó contra Liga, RFEF y evocó el Caso Negreira, y el equipo se quejó del doble rasero arbitral. Los blancos cinco amarillas y una roja tras cometer tan sólo ocho faltas, por las dos cartulinas tras 13 infracciones de sus rivales. Más allá de la intervención del VAR para sancionar la acción del brasileño, tras su inhibición en la famosa jugada de Fede Valverde y Kang-in Lee en el derbi previo a la pausa de selección. En Valdebebas, con Mou erigido en portavoz del club, se tiene claro que no se trata de hechos aislados. De hecho, la impresión es que poco o nada va a cambiar con relación al tratamiento arbitral hacia el club blanco. Que por su parte seguirá insistiendo en pedir reparaciones por el Caso Negreira. El Madrid va con todo en relación a una cuestión que ya está en manos de la UEFA, en quien los blancos confían para que se haga la justicia que se le sigue negando en el ámbito nacional. Así, el regreso de la Champions se presenta como un bálsamo para el Madrid, un oasis competitivo en comparación con el estrés que sufren los jugadores blancos en casi todas las jornadas de Liga. No hay partido fácil para el Madrid en España, algo que se atribuye más al contexto que rodea a la competición española que a aspectos estrictamente futbolísticos, aún asumiendo que el nivel del juego del equipo no está, hasta ahora, a la altura de lo esperado por la afición. La Champions, de hecho, ha sido la competición que más alegrías ha dado al madridismo en los últimos años. Se han ganado más Copas de Europa (seis desde 2014) que Ligas españolas (cuatro), una 'anomalía estadística' que puede entenderse como un argumento a favor del relato del club, expresado sobre todo a través de su canal oficial de TV. E incluso por Florentino Pérez, que ha aludido a este llamativo contraste en algunas de sus apariciones públicas. El conflicto con la UEFA por la Superliga, ya superado, no ha tenido incidencia directa en el trato hacia el Madrid en la máxima competición continental, la joya de la corona de las competiciones europeas. Así cree el Madrid que seguirá sucediendo pase lo que pase este miércoles en Roma. Un cambio de hábitat que el equipo agradece.

articles.title: Manchester City rule breaches: Enzo Maresca defends Anfield celebrations
articles.summary: Manager Enzo Maresca reacts to criticism of Manchester City's celebrations after their win at Liverpool by saying: "What do you want us to do?"
articles.body:
Head coach Enzo Maresca has reacted to criticism of Manchester City 's celebrations after their victory at Liverpool by saying: "What do you want us to do?"

Sunday's match at Anfield was City's first game after an independent commission found the club guilty of charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

After the 3-0 win, Erling Haaland looked close to tears in front of City's fans - which included his father Alf-Inge - while Maresca pumped his fists in jubilation.

"Criticised for what?" replied Maresca when asked for his response to City's celebrations being questioned by pundits and the media.

"We work every day to win games. It's the only thing that we can think about and be focused on.

"The rest? It's just things from outside that we need to deal with - but we were so, so, so happy on the pitch, and you cannot imagine inside the changing room."

The Italian added: "If I am an Arsenal fan or United fan and you are a City fan I say: 'hey, my friend you cheat'. So it is probably more tough for them [the fans], but we were happy inside the changing room.

"We were very happy celebrating the three points because it is very difficult at Anfield."

Maresca was speaking on Tuesday at a news conference before Wednesday's Champions League game with European champions Paris St-Germain.

It will be City's first match at home since the guilty verdict, which City have appealed against.

Captain Ruben Dias also defended the post-match celebrations at Anfield.

"I stand by the manager's words," said the centre-back. "It was a win at Anfield. It was a show of how much it means to us."

Asked for his reaction to the guilty verdict, the Portugal defender added: "We are very calm and we trust the club."

Pep Guardiola, who delivered 20 trophies during 10 years in charge before stepping aside at the end of last season, is expected to return to Etihad Stadium for the match.

"This has been his house for 10 years with what he has done here," added Maresca. "It's exciting for everyone, for the fans."

It is not known whether Guardiola will address the fans or his former players before the game.

The Spaniard posted a message on social media after his former club were found guilty of financial breaches.

"I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever," he wrote.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together."

articles.title: Mourinho ya está de vuelta
articles.standfirst: El entrenador volvió al Madrid con un talante conciliador pero ya tiene el relato para justificar su regreso al técnico más combativo
articles.summary: El entrenador regresó con un talante conciliador pero ya tiene el relato para justificar su regreso al técnico más combativo
articles.body: José Mourinho ha ido en las últimas semanas cambiando el discurso y recuperando su versión más combativa. "Me veo mucho más tranquilo. Desde hace años, no solamente ahora, siento que tengo más control con mis emociones", comentaba hace un mes. Y lo cierto es que así se vio en las ruedas de prensa, conciliador y reflexivo incluso con uno de los enemigos de su primera etapa, los medios de comunicación. Sin embargo, la rueda de prensa tras el polémico arbitraje en el derbi fue casi un antes y un después. Ya avisó tras la derrota ante el Betis, pero de forma tímida, hasta que apareció en El Metropolitano con el folio con la imagen de la entrada a Valverde. "Pensé que las cosas habían cambiado y que no eran como antes, pero ya me explicaron que no". El entrenador se preparaba para dar el giro, forzado también por las circunstancias adversas pero también un arbitraje pésimo. La rueda de prensa antes del la cita ante el Villarreal confirmó este extremo. A los árbitros como enemigo, hay que añadir de nuevo los medios de comunicación. Todo surge a raíz de la recuperación de Mbappé lejos de Valdebebas. Ya señala directamente a la prensa por una campaña "ridícula" y entiende que los pitos en el Bernabéu serían un triunfo de los periodistas. Su partido ante el Villareal desde el banquillo confirma este extremo. Mou, que hasta ahora se había mostrado más bien calmado desde su zona, está ya mucho más activo. Estuvo casi siempre de pie y mostró sus quejas de forma airada al cuarto árbitro. Incluso se resbaló una vez cuando se levantó rápido y saltó al césped tras la dura entrada de Foyth a Mbappé. El luso acabó con una amarilla que no le impidió seguir muy combativo. Pero la imagen del Mou de siempre llegó con el gol de Vinicius. El luso se metió una carrera de 40 metros mostrando su euforia hasta llegar al córner y abrazarse con el resto de jugadores. Quedaba una última maniobra que en su primera etapa ya hizo en alguna ocasión. No sentarse en la sala de prensa al final del partido. Lo que trascendió es que prefirió no hablar por miedo a que le sancionaran. En su primera aventura de blanco, el luso dejó en alguna ocasión que hablara Karanka, su segundo entonces, pero en esta ocasión no lo hizo nadie. Mourinho quiere que toda la responsabilidad de lo que ocurre en el Real Madrid recaiga en su figura. Cuando el Madrid está sufriendo para ganar, es una forma de proteger a sus jugadores. También es una forma de que la atención no se centre en las carencias del equipo. Buscar enemigos es una forma también de unir al Bernabéu en un frente común. El tiempo dirá si da resultados. El Madrid sigue inmerso en todos los frentes y al final de temporada será el momento de medir las responsabilidades, tanto ganando títulos como perdiendo.

articles.title: Sin novedades en la lista para Roma
articles.standfirst: Sólo se quedan fuera los lesionados de larga duración: Militao, Mendy y Rodrygo; vuelve Huijsen
articles.summary: Sólo se quedan fuera los lesionados de larga duración: Militao, Mendy y Rodrygo; vuelve Huijsen
articles.body: La vuelta de Dean Huijsen, que no jugó por sanción el partido del pasado sábado ante el Villarreal, es la única novedad en la lista de convocados del Real Madrid para el duelo de Champions de este miércoles ante la Roma (21.00 horas). articles.title: El Eibar vuelve a ser mortal: primera derrota en dos meses
articles.standfirst: Los armeros pusieron fin a su espectacular trayectoria tras otra mala puesta en escena y una reacción que no estuvo acompañada por la eficacia de otros partidos
articles.summary: Los armeros pusieron fin a su espectacular trayectoria tras otra mala puesta en escena y una reacción que no estuvo acompañada por la eficacia de otros partidos
articles.body: El Oviedo y el Carlos Tartiere pusieron fin a la mejor racha del Eibar en su historia en el fútbol profesional. Los armeros se quedaron con las ganas de encadenar su octavo triunfo y perdieron el liderato tras firmar un encuentro en el que, al igual que en Albacete, entraron mal al partido. Fueron a más con el paso de los minutos, pero esta vez le faltó la pegada de otras tardes para poder voltear el marcador y se topó con un gran Escandell. Era cuestión de tiempo que el Eibar pusiera fin a su racha de triunfos. El contador se detuvo en las siete victorias. Una trayectoria sobresaliente para un equipo que tampoco encontró la manera de traducir en demasiadas situaciones de gol sus fases de ataques en estático en una segunda mitad en la que el Oviedo le cedió la posesión. De hecho, casi todas las acciones de peligro, la mayoría en la primera mitad, llegaron con espacios para correr. El Eibar arrancó en Oviedo una parte del calendario claramente exigente. En apenas un mes se enfrentará a Mallorca, Castellón, Almería y Girona. Un momento de la temporada que marcará dónde puede estar el equipo de Jokin Aranbarri al final de temporada. No obstante, la derrota en el Tartiere tampoco cambia el rumbo de una plantilla que ha estado con los pies en el suelo en todo este tiempo y que ya piensa en la visita del sábado del Mallorca. Aranbarri sorprendió ayer en Oviedo dando toda la segunda mitad a Peru Nolaskoain. La tarjeta que vio Elgezabal en el primer tiempo le obligó a cubrirse en el descanso y apostar por la entrada del jugador de Zumaia, que formó pareja de baile con Arbilla en el eje de la zaga. Esta semana podría reaparecer Sergio Álvarez y Gift, lo que dejaría la enfermería sin efectivos y obligaría al técnico a realizar dos descartes. Todos los refuerzos son bienvenidos en esta fase del curso en el que vienen curvas.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti Jokes About Defending Jeremiah Smith in Video Ahead of Ohio State vs. Indiana
articles.summary: Indiana coach Curt Cignetti knows his team will have its hands full with Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.
articles.body:
Indiana coach Curt Cignetti knows his team will have its hands full with Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

He quipped on The Triple Option , an AMP Sports Original Series, the Hoosiers defense is "not allowed to play with 12 or 13" (34:40 mark).

"He's a great player. He's playing at another level," Cignetti said. "They're moving him around, and they're doing a great job with him. He's a wow guy. That's the only word I can think of when somebody asks me about him, is wow. So we got to do the best we can."

Smith has played Indiana twice, and the two meetings presented a strong contrast. As a freshman, he caught three passes for 34 yards in a 38-15 win over the Hoosiers. Last year, he had a much better individual performance (eight receptions for 144 yards), albeit in a losing effort.

The dynamic wideout has expanded his game as a junior. He ranks second nationally in catches (48), yards (916) and touchdowns (11). His numbers would be even higher if Ohio State hadn't had the luxury of dialing back his usage in blowout wins over Kent State and Maryland.

The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner mentioned Smith as joining Calvin Johnson and Julio Jones "among the best college receiver prospects we've seen this century."

This figures to be a game where Indiana will really miss 2025 All-American cornerback D'Angelo Ponds.

Neutralizing Smith altogether is probably out of the question. He's going to have an impact on Saturday in Bloomington.

For Cignetti and his staff, the objective is to prevent Smith from having the kind of monster performance that can swing the game in OSU's favor.

articles.title: World Cup 2030: Netflix wins rights to show matches in Spain
articles.summary: Netflix will broadcast World Cup games for the first time in 2030 as it secures the rights to show World Cup games in co-host Spain and Andorra.
articles.body:
Streaming platform Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup in Spain and Andorra.

It is the first time the subscription-based platform will show the men's World Cup.

"We will offer all 104 matches of the world's biggest football competition live," Netflix said in a statement.

Reigning champions Spain will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will also stage matches to celebrate the tournament's centenary.

The American subscription service said it was agreed "one game per match-day will be available to watch for free in Spain".

All of Spain's games and the final are among matches that will still be shown on free-to-air television, Netflix added.

Netflix has previously shown live sporting events in the UK - such as WWE Wrestling, NFL matches and boxing - and will broadcast the all-British heavyweight contest between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in December.

The company also holds the rights to the 2027 and 2031 editions of the women's World Cup in the United States and Canada.

articles.title: WNBA Considering Moving Finals Schedule, Allowing Dream to Play at Bigger Venue
articles.summary: The shift would let the Dream host games at a bigger venue.
articles.body:
The WNBA is heavily considering moving its Finals schedule, opening the door for the Atlanta Dream to host games at a bigger arena, a source familiar with the matter told Front Office Sports .

It's not immediately clear which Finals games will be moved, but Atlanta is scheduled to host Games 3, 4, and 6 on Oct. 22, 24, and 29, respectively.

The Dream have played their home playoff games at State Farm Arena, which fits about 17,000 fans. But the venue is booked out during its home Finals dates for a Sombr concert (Oct. 22) and regular-season games for the NBA's Hawks (Oct. 24 and 29).

Because of the schedule conflict, the Dream were expected to host Finals games at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center, their home arena since 2021. The Hawks operate State Farm Arena, which is owned by the Atlanta Fulton County Recreation Authority, and have played there since it opened in 1999.

The Dream have averaged about 9,700 fans at those home games.

State Farm Arena does not have any events scheduled Oct. 23, 26, 27, and 30, according to its website . A Dream spokesperson told FOS that the team is "still finalizing our home court venue."

A change in the date will also impact the WNBA Finals broadcast partners. NBC will air Games 1 and 4, while USA Network will air Games 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7.

A schedule change to Game 3 would move the game away from facing off against Thursday Night Football , while Game 4 of the WNBA Finals currently overlaps with Game 2 of the World Series. However, any move may still overlap with the World Series, which has games scheduled for Oct. 26, 27, 28, and 30.

articles.title: Série A club hit with three more transfer bans, taking total to seven
articles.summary: Santos have received three more transfer bans from FIFA, bringing their total to seven. The new sanctions stem from debts related to FIFA’s solidarity mechan...
articles.body:
Santos have received three more transfer bans from FIFA, bringing their total to seven. The new sanctions stem from debts related to FIFA's solidarity mechanism, according to ge.

According to the report, one of the debts amounts to US$55,000 (around R$275,000). The other two total €120,000 (approximately R$671,000).

Until these amounts are paid, Santos cannot register new signings. In practice, the club were already banned for up to three transfer windows over a debt owed to former Santos coach Pedro Caixinha.

Last week, the club received four transfer bans over debts to the Portuguese coach and his three assistants, totaling more than R$15 million.

In addition to the seven active transfer bans, another sanction could be on the way, according to ge. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld FIFA's ruling against Santos over a debt of around R$2.2 million owed to Qatar's Al-Markhiya. The decision was published on Monday.

The Gambian striker joined on loan in the second half of 2024, with a deal running until June 2025. He spent four months at the club, did not play a single match and was sent back at the end of that year.

articles.title: Champions League still ultimate ambition for Bayern Munich, Harry Kane
articles.summary: FC Bayern is on a mission.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich enjoyed a trophy-filled campaign last season, but Harry Kane knows there is still one prize that stands above the rest for the German giants: the Champions League.

After helping Bayern secure three domestic trophies last season, the England captain is optimistic about the club's chances of making a serious run at European glory this year. With Vincent Kompany's squad continuing to develop and several quality additions strengthening the team, Kane believes Bayern has the tools to challenge for the biggest prize in European club football.

Speaking about his Champions League ambitions for the season, Kane emphasized the importance of building on last year's success while improving in the decisive moments that determine a team's fate in the competition.

"Winning the three trophies here in Germany [last season], it was a special season in that sense. The Champions League is always the ultimate goal, always the target for this club and for me, so going into this season I think we have a great opportunity. A lot of the players now have been working with Vincent Kompany for a while; we've added some great additions as well," Kane told UEFA (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). "Right now, it's just about making sure we finish as high as possible in the league phase. But, yeah, I'm feeling optimistic. I think we've proven over the last couple of years that we can be really dangerous. The goals we've scored as a team last year [were] record breaking as well. So we need a lot of the same things plus just that little bit more in the final moments – maybe a few decisions to go our way, these little details that matter."

Kane's comments highlight both Bayern's confidence and the fine margins that can separate Champions League winners from teams left wondering what might have been. Bayern demonstrated their attacking potential last season with a record-breaking goal tally, but converting that dominance into European success requires consistency, composure, and the ability to deliver under the greatest pressure.

The league phase will be an important first step, with Bayern looking to secure the strongest possible position before the knockout rounds begin. From there, the challenge will be navigating the competition's toughest tests, where a single moment can decide an entire season.

For Kane, the motivation is clear. Domestic success is important, but the Champions League remains the ultimate ambition for both the striker and his club. With Kompany's project continuing to take shape, Bayern will be hoping this is the season they finally put everything together and bring European football's biggest club prize back to Munich.

articles.title: Mourinho identifies four Real Madrid players as key to beating AS Roma – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid will be looking to secure all three points as they take on AS Roma in the UEFA Champions League tomorrow night.It will be a litmus test for coach...
articles.body:
Real Madrid will be looking to secure all three points as they take on AS Roma in the UEFA Champions League tomorrow night.

It will be a litmus test for coach Jose Mourinho against one of his former teams, and securing a win could be crucial, given Real Madrid's recent run of inconsistent performances.

Aware of the pressure, Mourinho now wants most of his players to play to their full potential heading into midweek's game against Roma.

As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho has identified Roma's high press as the biggest threat his side will face at the Stadio Olimpico, and has concluded that four men in particular must rise to the occasion to beat it.

Mourinho is well aware of AS Roma's strengths. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Having coached Roma himself not long ago, the Portuguese knows exactly how dangerous their pressing can be, and he is acutely aware that playing out from the back is where Real Madrid have looked most vulnerable this season.

The first name on his list is Thibaut Courtois. Mourinho wants the Belgian to act as Madrid's first playmaker, using his footwork and distribution to pick the right option whenever the team recycles possession back to him.

Alongside him, Dean Huijsen is expected to be pivotal. The centre-back's ability to break lines with vertical passes, allied to his composure on the ball, could prove invaluable in bypassing Roma's initial wave of pressure.

The other two men entrusted with the task operate slightly higher up the pitch.

Trent Alexander-Arnold's range of passing, his knack for switching play and finding teammates between the lines, makes him a natural outlet down the right.

Tchouameni must be incisive in the middle of the park. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

Even if Mourinho opts for Denzel Dumfries from the start, the Englishman's quality later in the game could still prove decisive.

Completing the quartet is Aurelien Tchouameni, whose job will be to link defence and midfield. His physicality allows him to shield the ball under pressure, while a single incisive pass through the first line could release Bellingham or Arda Guler into promising areas.

The message from Mourinho is clear. The forwards will carry the individual quality, but the foundation for a result in Rome must be laid in Madrid's own penalty area.

articles.title: Manchester United are in the race to sign giant 24-year-old striker
articles.summary: Manchester United Tracking Dion Beljo as January Striker Plans Take ShapeManchester United are among the clubs keeping a close eye on Dinamo Zagreb striker D...
articles.body:
Manchester United Tracking Dion Beljo as January Striker Plans Take Shape

Manchester United are among the clubs keeping a close eye on Dinamo Zagreb striker Dion Beljo ahead of the January transfer window, according to TeamTalk , with Tottenham and Everton also following the Croatian forward's progress.

Beljo, 24, has moved into the spotlight after a blistering spell in front of goal. The report states that the 6ft 5in striker has scored "12 goals in his last 14 games", a run that includes "10 in seven league appearances for Dinamo Zagreb", while he has also scored for Croatia. Those numbers explain why Premier League recruitment departments are paying such close attention.

The current situation appears to be one of strong monitoring rather than an advanced negotiation. As reported, "the interest in Beljo remains at the tracking and assessment stage", with clubs still gathering information before deciding whether to act. Even so, the level of attention around him feels significant, especially with January "emerging as a potential opening for the Premier League trio to consider their options".

Beljo's record stretches beyond a brief purple patch. The article points out that his "38-goal return across 48 appearances last season" suggests there is more here than a temporary burst of confidence. For clubs searching for value in a difficult market, that consistency matters. His profile also stands out, a physically imposing centre-forward with clear momentum and growing international recognition.

Brentford are also credited with interest, while the report adds that both the City Football Group and BlueCo have shown attention. Newcastle United and Leeds United have been linked too, giving this story the feel of a developing market rather than a single-club push.

Manchester United striker search continues

From a United perspective, the logic is easy to follow. The report says "Man Utd are open to bringing in a new forward to compete with the likes of Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha, while Joshua Zirkzee's future at Old Trafford remains in doubt." That line is especially telling. It suggests the club's thinking is not only about adding depth, but also about planning for possible movement in the squad.

United's recruitment in attack has come under repeated scrutiny in recent windows, so any move for Beljo would likely be judged on two levels, immediate impact and longer-term upside. His current form is impossible to ignore, and the market often moves quickly once a striker starts producing at this rate.

Premier League rivals remain in the frame

Tottenham and Everton both have clear reasons to explore the opportunity. TeamTalk notes that Spurs have seen their "need for a new striker" increase, while Everton are described as "arguably the club most in need of a new forward." In short, United may have company if Beljo becomes genuinely available.

For now, this is a situation to watch rather than one on the verge of completion. Still, when a striker is described as "one of the most talked-about forwards in European football", it usually means decisions are getting closer.

As a Manchester United supporter, this is the kind of link that immediately sparks curiosity. Dion Beljo sounds like a market opportunity rather than a glamorous headline signing, and sometimes that is exactly where the best business gets done. When you read "12 goals in his last 14 games" and then see "38-goal return across 48 appearances last season", it feels like due diligence would be the bare minimum.

The big question is whether he is being tracked as a genuine option for the first-team squad or simply as one of several names on a long shortlist. United have signed forwards on reputation before, so there is something refreshing about the idea of targeting a player whose case is being built on output, profile and development potential.

There is also the squad angle. If "Joshua Zirkzee's future at Old Trafford remains in doubt", then bringing in another striker starts to make more sense. United need competition, presence in the box and someone who can offer a different dynamic. Beljo's size alone suggests he could bring that.

Supporters will naturally want a bigger name, but smart recruitment is about fit and timing. If United believe Beljo can adapt quickly and continue his rise, then January could be a very sensible moment to act before the price climbs and the queue gets even longer.

articles.title: Josh Pate, John Fanta Blast CFP Expansion: ‘Why Stop at 24?’
articles.summary: The deadline for College Football Playoff expansion in 2027 is Dec. 1, 2026.
articles.body:
There's growing momentum for an expanded College Football Playoff. Last month, the CFP issued a statement announcing its officially considering expansion to 24 teams, while launching a 30-day negotiating window with ESPN. However, influential media members question if expansion will stop there.

NBC Sports broadcaster John Fanta and Josh Pate, host of Josh Pate's College Football Show and contributing analyst at ESPN, slammed the idea of expansion at the Front Office Sports Tuned In summit Tuesday morning.

"We're going to call it an expanded playoff," Pate said. "Really, what it is is it's an ATM to bail out very bad decision-making from, and I use this term loosely, leadership in college football."

The formal deadline for whether the CFP will expand to 24 teams for the 2027 season is on Dec. 1; if an agreement is not reached, then it will remain at 12 teams next season.

Fanta's seen expansion in another sport he covers: college basketball. The NCAA tournament has expanded from 64 teams to 68 in recent years and will debut a 76-team field this upcoming season. When asked his opinion by Front Office Sports' s Ryan Glasspiegel, he wonders if the CFP will follow a similar trend of continued growth.

"The effort's going to be there, the pageantry, the theater of it's going to be there," Fanta said. "I get all those things, and I love that about college football. I think college football is really fun, but we have barely given 12 teams time and runway. The moment that it goes to 12, we say 24. When it goes to 24, are we going to try to go to 30?"

Pate quickly quipped back, adding to Fanta's point.

"For all of these reasons that you would expand to 24, I keep looking, and I keep saying, why would you stop at 24?" Pate said. "Why not go to 36? It's the college basketball effect, but it's just in college football."

The College Football Playoff debuted in 2014 with four teams. The field expanded to 12 teams after the 2023 season and has changed in each subsequent season.

In 2024, the four highest-ranked conference champions received first-round byes. In 2025, the seeding protocol changed, and the 12 qualifying teams were ranked from highest to lowest. This year, the Power 4 conferences will each be guaranteed a spot for their conference champion, along with one spot for the highest-ranked team from the Group of 6 (formerly the Group of 5). Last season's ACC champion, Duke, was left out after a 7-5 regular season.

While comparing the two sports, Fanta acknowledged that expansion in basketball seems more practical than football. The variance in the NCAA tournament over its history lends itself to more upsets and parity. Conversely, the average margin of victory in the first round of College Football Playoff games in the first two years of the 12-team era has been nearly 18 points per game.

"Basketball is different than football. It just is," Fanta said. "You can come out, and you can go 10 for your first 13 from (three-point range) and be involved in the game. In college football, the game is won and lost in the trenches, and we're seeing it in a lot of these first-round college football playoff games.

"I don't think there's nearly as much of a difference between (the 75th team and the 55th team) in college basketball. There's a difference in college football, a significant one."

Despite public criticisms, industry leaders feel a 24-team CFP is inevitable at some point. More than expanded access and parity, Pate believes the idea is being pushed through to increase revenue and viewership.

"The movers in college football are even going so far as to acknowledge publicly, 'We know that fan support, or sentiment rather, is against this," Pate said. "It's almost that 'Well, you'll watch anyway'. You know, you'll take what we give you anyway. But in the aggregate, we've really screwed this up nine ways from Sunday. We need a bailout. We've got to create revenue somewhere."

articles.title: Beat writer discusses 'formula' the Vikings have found to win in 2026
articles.summary: A dominant defense and special teams unit have carried the Vikings to a 5-0 start.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, only one of three undefeated teams after Week 5. Their offense accumulated 364 yards in Sunday's win over the New Orleans Saints , but Minnesota still ranks 27th in yards. Two Vikings fumbles in the red zone kept the Saints in the game longer than they should have, but Minnesota still prevailed 23-13.

Although the Vikings' offense was good, the defense was even better, as it has been all season. Brian Flores dialed up pressure on Tyler Shough all day, limiting New Orleans to 142 yards in the win. It was the second straight week Minnesota held its opponent under 200 total yards, and they haven't allowed over 300 yards in a game since Week 1.

Three field goals by Will Reichard helped the Vikings build a two-score lead, with kicks from 40, 54, and 55 yards. That combination gives ESPN's Kevin Seifert reason to believe this team can outperform expectations from analytic models, which don't rate Minnesota as highly as their 5-0 record would suggest.

Few projected the Vikings to spend much time atop the NFC North, and even after starting the season with four consecutive wins, they still ranked No. 14 in ESPN's Football Power Index. But they have a formula that is working and has given them a two-game lead in the division -- which includes two NFC North wins and four in the conference. Their offense continues to mystify, losing two red-zone fumbles Sunday. But their defense has locked down opponents all season; the Saints managed just 142 total yards. Kicker Will Reichard brought his season conversion total to 15-for-15 with three more field goals, including one from 55 and another from 54.

The Vikings have a bye in Week 6, giving Kevin O'Connell a chance to self-scout and improve on an offense that is improving but is still inconsistent. If Kyler Murray and the offense keep making strides after their bye week, Minnesota has a chance to be a true contender.

articles.title: Krystian Bielik: Cardiff defender makes death threat claim following fan clash
articles.summary: Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik claims his family received death threats amid the controversy that surrounded his altercation with a Portsmouth fan.
articles.body:
Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik claimed his family received death threats amid the controversy that surrounded his altercation with a Portsmouth fan.

Bielik was banned for two games and fined £10,000 for the incident during the clubs' Championship meeting at Fratton Park last month.

The 28-year-old Poland international admitted a charge of misconduct after he was deemed to have grabbed the young fan by the shoulder.

Bielek made contact with the fan having gone to retrieve the ball for a throw-in during the second half of Cardiff's 2-1 defeat.

Cardiff warned of struggle - but is criticism fair?

A Hampshire Police investigation into the flashpoint concluded that no further action was needed, with Bielik being issued a Community Resolution Order.

He also sent a written apology to the fan before he was charged by the FA.

Bielik's disciplinary case was heard by an independent regulatory commission last week, with full written reasons for the verdict revealing the defender's claim that his family had been subjected to death threats.

The assertion formed part of Bielik's plea for mitigation, and was described by the commission as "regrettable and to be deplored" but said it did not impact on the sanction "particularly as no supporting evidence had been provided".

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy also provided support, describing the 11-time Poland international as a "consummate professional".

In his own statement, Bielik described how he had expected the ball to be handed to him by the fan and claimed "[I] placed my hand on his shoulder and pushed away as I moved back", before adding his actions were caused partly by frustration and also by momentum.

That was disputed by the FA, who said the proximity of the contact to the neck risked inflaming the crowd, something the commission agreed with, adding the incident "clearly created the potential for a mass confrontation and could have led to a dangerous situation".

Bielik admitted his regret and argued that he did not retaliate despite being struck in the face during the incident. The commission said this was commendable but "could not lessen his culpability for his initial action", although they accepted other mitigating factors in reducing the ban from the three-game starting point.

articles.summary: Joel Sánchez, Fitzgerald y Gross firman tres obras de arte
articles.body: Hay algo que se ha convertido en un denominador común en casi todas las categorías de la Academia del Atlético y es el talento de sus jugadores. El Juvenil que participa en la Youth League no iba a ser la excepción. El equipo de Pedro Moya suma una gran cantidad de futbolistas ofensivos en los que hay muchas esperanzas puestas. El duelo ante el United de la segunda jornada fue una muestra clara de ello. Joel Sánchez, Fitzgerald y Gross se inventaron tres golazos para tumbar a los ‘red devils’. Alcalá pudo disfrutar de tres auténticas obras de arte para colocar a los rojiblancos con cuatro puntos en sus dos primeros partidos de la competición. Buena pinta la de este puñado de jóvenes talentosos. Un triunfo que da buena muestra del potencial que tiene este equipo. El primero fue una jugada individual de Joel Sánchez. El extremo firmó su segundo tanto de la competición con una gran acción por el costado izquierdo. Tras conducir, su golpeo desde fuera del área se coló en la portería de Byrne-Hughes. El Atlético se ponía por delante a los diez minutos y encarrilaba el choque. Pudo llegar el segundo pero el meta británico despachó dos paradones para evitar el tanto rojiblanco. Poco pudo hacer en el golpe de Fitzgerald. El atacante colchonero despachó un gol espectacular tras un gran jugada de Javi Tena. El centrocampista reconvertido en central en línea de tres aprovechó su zancada para llevar la pelota prácticamente al área rival. El balón acabó en los pies de Fitzgerald que la puso en la escuadra. El Atlético ponía tierra de por medio antes de llegar al descanso. El segundo acto dejó un United más atrevido en busca de recortar distancias. Cuanto más apretaban los ingleses apareció una cabalgada de Gross disfrazado de Messi. Tras tumbar a varios rivales acabó anotando el tercer tanto rojiblanco pisando ya el área inglesa. Tercer tanto, tercera obra de arte. El Atlético despachaba así el partido con tres auténticos golazos para mirar hacia arriba en la Youth League. articles.title: Juan Manuel arranca con fuerza: "Conmigo nadie tiene garantizado el puesto"
articles.standfirst: Se hace cargo del primer equipo de Las Palmas 14 años después
articles.summary: Se hace cargo del primer equipo de Las Palmas 14 años después
articles.body: Primeras horas de Juan Manuel Rodríguez al frente del primer equipo de la UD Las Palmas. El hasta ahora técnico del filial no ha escondido la ilusión que tiene en esta nueva etapa, aunque sea transitoria: "me han explicado la situación, que ellos buscan un nuevo técnico. Soy hombre de club y no he dudado en aceptar la propuesta". Aunque la última vez que entrenó a un equipo profesional data del año 2012, el inquilino del banquillo se siente con fuerzas: "Nadie es la misma persona y entrenador que hace equis años. Todo el mundo evoluciona". También ha reconocido que apenas ha pegado ojo desde que supo la noticia: "No he dormido observando y viendo. Desconozco la situación de lesionados o recuperados. Próximamente diremos más cosas bajo el conocimiento más concreto de la realidad". Eso sí, ha dejado claro que con él al mando "nadie tiene garantizado el puesto". Se sentará en el banquillo ante el Castellón, pero no sabe hasta cuándo: "Las Palmas no tiene que decirme nada: me elige o me quita cuando sea conveniente. Soy hombre de club y respeto todos los acontecimientos que se dan". Juan Manuel llega a un vestuario nuevo para él, aunque admite que tiene un plan: "Mi idea es la de buscar un equilibrio: saber defender y saber atacar. ¿Qué es jugar bien? Es hacer en todo lo momento lo que toca hacer. Eso para mí es jugar bien. Hay que ser solidarios, porque el bloque está por encima de cualquier individualidad" Por su parte, el director deportivo Luis Helguera agradeció el trabajo y la profesionalidad de Rubén de la Barrera: "es un gran profesional y una buena persona, que se ha entregado y ha hecho todo lo que ha podido". El diseñador de la plantilla del equipo para la temporada 2026-27 añadió que "no hemos sido capaces de tener buenos resultados". Helguera también dio la bienvenida a Juan Manuel Rodríguez y aclaró que el técnico grancanario llega "de manera transitoria" al banquillo insular. "Estamos contentos, conocemos el perfil de entrenador, es de la casa, y vamos apoyarle y a ayudarle en todo lo que quiera", señaló.

articles.title: 'State of the Game': Independent Football Regulator's report finds most English clubs living on financial brink
articles.summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has produced a 'State of the Game' report which has taken a forensic look at English football over the past 18 months concluding that the game's finances are dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster.
articles.body:
The IFR added that interest and investment from around the world continues to grow within English football, but the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform.

Despite over £9bn generated in revenue, 94 per cent of clubs are loss-making, with long-term security being put at risk through excessive short-term spending to keep up with rivals. This, the IFR says, has led to a "dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".

The report acknowledges that the success of the Premier League has driven economic success, making English football the "richest, best and most deeply competitive in the world".

However, it points to "financial cliff-edges between and within leagues", with the average Premier League club making more than eight times the revenues of an average Championship club, and the system of parachute payments paid by the Premier League to Championship clubs relegated contributing to significant overspend by clubs in the Championship.

Indeed, the report highlights player wage inflation leading clubs to take big risks chasing a place in the Premier League.

The State of the Game report found that lower down the pyramid the pressure from operating costs was also on the rise, with 17 EFL and National League clubs incurring costs exceeding revenues. These clubs would be loss-making even if they did not pay their players.

It uncovered too that more than 60 per cent of EFL and National League clubs are technically insolvent, with their liabilities exceeding the book value of their assets.

And it found that more than a quarter of clubs would be unable to survive for more than one month if owner funding was withdrawn, with the majority lacking a basic contingency plan to mitigate their risk.

'We're trying to take an interventionist approach'

Chair of the IFR David Kogan told Sky : "I think what we see in English football is two completely different positions.

"The first is £9bn comes in every year, yet we have 94 per cent of the clubs of the 160 we regulate are trading unprofitably.

"We have 32 clubs that have got less than 30 days' cash cover in their accounts. So if the owner walks away or drops dead, they're insolvent and go bust.

"So what we see in football is rising debt. It's a problem of cash cover and liquidity within clubs, and it's a lack of management, and what financial management? And now we're in a position to help those clubs achieve a more stable future."

Kogan added: "What we're implying is today there's enough money going through into the Premier League and the EFL and into their individual clubs for the sun to shine. This is exactly the moment when we need to address structural issues because once that sun stops shining, those clubs will be in real trouble.

"So what we are trying to do is get ahead of the problem and take an interventionist approach with individual clubs that need it to help them get to the point of being stable and secure because too many clubs get close to the edge and depend on one thing and one thing only, which is a new owner coming down the track.

"That supply of owners may dry up, and supply of media money may dry out so we have to now get ahead of the game and give them levels of security and stability that allow them to go into the future."

The IFR report offered solutions, issuing a six-point plan to address some of the issues it has identified.

The plan includes measures for clubs to improve how they manage financial risk, including holding more cash and putting robust contingency plans in place in case owner funding is withdrawn; it also outlines how revenue distribution should be reformed to ease cliff-edges throughout the pyramid, urges action on rising losses and calls on clubs to show how they take fans' views into account, and the steps they are taking to improve diversity and governance in the boardroom.

It also highlighted yet again that the current distribution arrangements in English football create risk and should be reformed.

For several years the Premier League and EFL have been discussing and negotiating a new financial distribution model, but no agreement has yet been finalised. The IFR has consistently said, and has said once again in this report, that it is preferable that the Premier League and EFL come to an agreement themselves, but again mentioned that the IFR could apply a "back-stop" power to intervene if the Premier League and EFL do not come to an agreement.

The IFR said its goals on reform of the current distribution model were to:

Maintain the Premier League as the leading football league in the world and the Championship as the leading second-tier competition.

Maintain vital funding for the wider game.

Mitigate the financial impact of relegation from the Premier League.

Reduce the distortive impact that parachute payments have on financial incentives within the Championship.

Protect clubs by giving clubs the opportunity to rebuild their balance sheets and reduce risk.

Consider short-term support to clubs that face severe financial distress.

Kogan said: "There are three moves that are taking place that we think will help on this.

"First is that the Premier League and the EFL are currently discussing a new distribution deal with the game, which will radically change the amount of money going from the Premier League down to the lower leagues. And that will have associated with it controls on how that money is spent, which actually will go to the stability of those lower leagues, but we're going to see more money flowing down, assuming the deal is done, and we're going to see cost controls involved in that.

"The second is that from November onwards we're going to be licensing clubs, and by licensing those clubs we're going to intervene directly in individual clubs where we think they've got exposures that we can help them resolve and that includes things like having a business plan that involves having cash cover more than 30 days; it involves having genuine provision for the debts that they've raised.

"And the third thing we're doing is working with leagues to actually look at cost controls over a longer-term basis to actually build in financial stability as we go forward."
